Title: Scam syndicates prepared fake passports, flight tickets to flee Malaysia
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The two foreign online scam syndicates crippled in Seri Kembangan and Jalan Kerinchi had prepared forged passports and flight tickets to flee the country if their activities were exposed to enforcement authorities.
The syndicates were busted by the Immigration Department following two raids yesterday and this morning.
A total of 34 foreigners were detained during a raid on four luxury condominium units in Jalan Kerinchi, while another 30 were arrested during a separate operation at two bungalows in The Mines, Seri Kembangan.
Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said investigators discovered three passport booklets bearing the names of Japan, South Korea and the United States, raising suspicions that syndicate members had made advance preparations to flee.
He said the documents, which had yet to be printed with the holders' particulars, were recovered during special operations against online scam activities in the Klang Valley.

Title: Sanusi: Singapore has 'Singlish', I am from Sik... we have 'Siklish'
Article:
ALOR STAR: Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has defended his command of the English language at the recent SG4 Business and Economic Forum.
He said communication skills should not be assessed solely based on grammatical accuracy, but rather on how effectively a message is conveyed to the audience.
He added that he had never been criticised by native English speakers, only by Malaysians social media users.
"All those who have commented are Malays. The United States ambassador (to Malaysia) and high commissioners of Australia, Canada and India, when I speak to them, they understand, they appreciate me... that is the art of communication." he said after a lecture programme on "The Greater Kedah".
He said this in response to social media users' criticism of his use of English when he raised the issue of rare earth elements (REE) at the SG4 forum.
SG4 is the collective of the four states — Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan and Terengganu — that are held by Perikatan Nasional.
Sanusi said he had travelled to 38 countries where he had used English to communicate with local leaders.
He said he did not consider grammatical accuracy an absolute measure of communication, as long as the message conveyed could be understood by the recipient.
"Every language is important, but performance and the way a message is delivered are even more important. As long as people understand and accept it, then praise God.
"Communication is not something that can be measured with a ruler. There is no need to be overly rigid about correctness.
"As long as people understand, that is fine. I am from Sik, so we have the Sik dialect, which becomes 'Siklish', just as Singapore has 'Singlish'," he said.
On the issue REEs, he said he hoped the federal government would expedite the formulation of policies on the mining of these minerals to enable states with such resources to generate new sources of revenue.
He said investors had already expressed interest in investing in REE exploration and processing activities, but the process of obtaining mining licences continued to face constraints related to policy and technical approvals.
"Please expedite the formulation of the policy. We want to extract REE. Investors have already come in to conduct exploration, and once the exploration process is completed, we want to issue mining licences.
"However, they need to prepare mining plans, conduct environmental impact assessments (EIAs) and fulfil various other requirements that depend on policies and approvals. When the technical process is slow, extraction is delayed, and the state's new revenue is also held up," he said.
He said delays risked causing the state to miss out on opportunities to capitalise on the current high demand for REE, which has the potential to become a new source of revenue.

Title: HeiTech Padu clarifies Zetrix AI teaming agreement, both parties agreed not to extend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: HeiTech Padu Bhd today clarified that the Teaming Agreement it entered into with Zetrix AI Bhd on April 16, 2024, was an interim collaboration to explore potential opportunities to provide information technology services in Malaysia.
However, the agreement has since lapsed, and both parties have mutually agreed not to extend it, the company said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
"Accordingly, there is no ongoing collaboration between HeiTech Padu and Zetrix in relation to the National Integrated Immigration System (NIISe) project pursuant to the Teaming Agreement.
"The lapse of the agreement does not have any material impact on the implementation and delivery of the NIISe project," the company added.
HeiTech Padu was responding to news reports that the collaboration between the two companies on NIISe had lapsed.
On the Supplemental Agreement signed with Zetrix on Aug 4, 2025, HeiTech Padu said it was intended to record both parties' understanding of their respective obligations and roles under the original Teaming Agreement.
As at the date of the announcement, HeiTech Padu had no ongoing projects requiring collaboration with Zetrix under the Supplemental Agreement, it said.

Title: Two scam syndicates collect RM6mil in 2 months, 64 arrested
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Two online scam syndicates believed to have raked in RM6 million in just two months have been crippled following raids on luxury condominiums and bungalows in the Klang Valley, with 64 foreigners arrested.
The syndicates, which operated from four luxury condominium units in Jalan Kerinchi, Kuala Lumpur, and two bungalows in The Mines, Seri Kembangan, were generating between RM100,000 and RM150,000 daily by targeting victims through fraudulent investment schemes and offers of non-existent services.
Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the two-day operation on Oct 28 and 29 resulted in the arrest of 44 Chinese nationals, 19 Vietnamese nationals and one Myanmar national.
He said the syndicates, which had been operating for about two months, had collected more than RM60,000 today alone, based on transaction records recovered from their computers.

Title: Pahang's RM850mil Chereh Dam solar project to create 1,500 jobs
Article:
KUANTAN: A RM850 million floating solar photovoltaic (PV) project at Chereh Dam in Pahang is expected to create about 1,500 jobs and generate clean electricity equivalent to the annual consumption of 100,000 households.
Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah said the project, a collaboration between Citaglobal Bhd, Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC (Masdar) and Tiza Global Sdn Bhd, marked a major step towards expanding the state's use of renewable energy.
The Pahang Ruler said the project was set to become one of the largest floating solar installations in Southeast Asia, while creating employment opportunities for local communities.
"We hope it will create jobs and be completed as soon as possible," Al-Sultan Abdullah told reporters after officiating at the groundbreaking ceremony for the Chereh Dam floating solar PV project at a hotel here today.
Citaglobal Bhd group chief operating officer Datuk Aimi Aizal Nasharuddin said construction was expected to begin in January or February next year, with completion targeted for the end of March 2028.
The 200-megawatt (MW) project will cover about 1,500 acres (607 hectares) of the dam's water surface and is expected to generate 1,500 jobs, particularly during the construction phase, he said.
The jobs would span several fields, including engineering, construction, hydrographic surveying, electrical engineering and other related professions.
Meanwhile, Citaglobal New Energy Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Chairil Nazri Ahmad said floating solar technology could improve electricity generation efficiency because panels installed over water generally operate at lower temperatures than those mounted on land.
He said installing solar panels on the reservoir could also help reduce water evaporation and preserve water reserves.
"The solar panels are estimated to have a total capacity of 307 MW, while the maximum electricity export capacity to the grid is 200 MW. Actual generation will depend on weather conditions and the amount of sunlight received, with the electricity generated fed into the grid for distribution to consumers," he said.
Also present were Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail, Citaglobal Bhd executive chairman and president Tan Sri Mohamad Norza Zakaria, and Masdar executive director for projects and business development Abdulla Zayed.

Title: Ahmad Shahazan Yacob elected MIA's new president, former Bursa chief Umar Swift is VP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Institute of Accountants (MIA) has elected Ahmad Syahazan Yaacob as its new president and Datuk Muhamad Umar Swift as vice-president effective today.
Ahmad succeeds Datuk Saniza Said, whose tenure as president ended on Sept 26, 2026.
He was appointed to the MIA Council on Sept 23, 2023, before being elected vice-president on Dec 8, 2025.
MIA said the appointments were confirmed at its council meeting on Oct 29.
Ahmad is currently the managing partner of Al Jafree Salihin Kuzaimi PLT, with extensive experience in audit and assurance involving listed and non-listed companies across various industries, including technology, plantation, oil and gas, construction and manufacturing.
He previously spent 10 years in audit and assurance with "Big Four" accounting firms and is a fellow of CPA Australia.
Meanwhile, Umar, who joined the MIA council on Sept 15, is the group chief executive officer of Qualitas Health Group.
He has more than 25 years of experience in banking and financial services, including senior leadership roles at Bursa Malaysia Bhd.
Umar also serves as vice-president of the Malaysian Institute of Certified Public Accountants and Asia regional councillor of Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand.
"MIA congratulates Ahmad and Umar on their election as president and vice president respectively.
"MIA looks forward to their leadership in advancing a future-ready, value-driven and trust-centred accountancy profession, upholding ethics, good governance and integrity, safeguarding public interest and supporting sustainable nation building," it said.

Title: MACC orders ex-Yayasan Bank Rakyat chairman, brother to declare assets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has ordered former Yayasan Bank Rakyat chairman Datuk Seri Nazir Hussin Akhtar Hussin and his elder brother, Datuk Mubarak Hussain Akhtar Husin, to declare their assets.
Both men were issued asset declaration notices on Oct 20, with Nazir understood to have received his at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya.
Mubarak was served at his residence.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed that both men had received and accepted the notices issued under Section 36 of the MACC Act.
He told the New Straits Times that they had 30 days to declare their assets, with a possible 30-day extension upon request.
Under Section 36, MACC may require individuals to furnish information on their assets, including movable and immovable property, financial holdings and other interests.
Investigators may also seek explanations on the sources of funds used to acquire assets to determine whether their wealth is consistent with known sources of income.
Earlier this month, Nazir
spent about two hours
at the MACC headquarters in connection with the asset declaration notice.
He later said his legal team had filed an injunction application at the Kuala Lumpur High Court to challenge the notice and prevent MACC from enforcing it.
Nazir said he could still be arrested despite the pending application and urged the commission to respect the legal process.
On Oct 1, MACC arrested
Nazir and Mubarak
in connection with an investigation into alleged collusion and abuse of power involving an investment of about RM10 million.
Initial investigations found that the two allegedly colluded with an officer of an education-based foundation to approve the investment in a company owned by the elder brother of one of the suspects in late 2020.
MACC also seized 15 luxury cars, 12 high-powered motorcycles, five luxury watches, three bracelets and about RM30,000 in cash.

Title: Sanusi: Pas to contest two seats in Melaka election
Article:
ALOR STAR: Pas will field candidates in two seats in the upcoming Melaka election, with another five seats being contested by other Perikatan Nasional component parties.
PN election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said these would include Gerakan and Parti Wawasan Rakyat.
However, he did not elaborate on how many seats the two other parties would contest.
"Pas has two seats. Gerakan and Wawasan have seats (to contest). I can only confirm Pas (has two seats).
"I will be there on nomination day on Saturday. I will be there to help (in the campaign)," he said after a lecture programme on "The Greater Kedah".
On the candidates to be fielded by Pas, he said the party would select candidates who possess the necessary qualifications, experience and potential to win the election.
Yesterday, Barisan Nasional and PN signed a
pact on political cooperation
in the Melaka election, with the former contesting 21 seats and the latter going for the remaining seven.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day, with Nov 10 set for early voters.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CSA unrelated to Bersatu-PH cooperation in Melaka, says Muhyiddin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) signed with the government had no connection to any electoral pact with Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the Melaka election.
Asked by reporters whether Bersatu would form an electoral pact with PH in Melaka, he said: "That's another question. Today, this has no connection here."
He was speaking after signing the agreement at Parliament here with several other Bersatu members of Parliament, including Datuk Seri Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Datuk Ali Biju (Saratok), Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Mohd Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai).
Asked whether the CSA would also apply to a similar agreement being sought between Bersatu and the PH-led Selangor government, he gave a similar answer.
"That's another question. This is between the federal government - the prime minister - and the members of Parliament representing my party and other parties," he said.
Those spotted at the signing also included Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin and Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.
Earlier, the government and several opposition MPs signed the agreement. Deputy Prime Ministers Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, as well as Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz, were also present.
Under the agreement, the MPs pledged to support the 2027 Budget and institutional reforms, including limiting the prime minister's tenure to a maximum of two terms and separating the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor.
The government, meanwhile, agreed to provide opposition MPs with development allocations equal to those given to government MPs from today and to cover the Bumiputera agenda.
An online portal previously reported that Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari had said a CSA would be signed with Bersatu before the Selangor Budget was tabled next month, subject to approval from PH's top leadership.
The Melaka
state election
will be held on Nov 14, with nomination on Oct 31.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesian police probe 97 corporations over forest fires, 20 named as suspects
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesian police are investigating 97 corporations, including 22 foreign-linked companies, over forest and land fire cases across the country, with 20 companies already named as suspects.
National Police Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) chief Comm Gen Asep Safrudin said 16 of the 20 corporate suspects were domestically invested companies, while the remaining four were foreign-invested.
"The number of corporate suspects may increase as our investigations continue," he said at a press conference in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, on Thursday, which was streamed live on social media.
Asep said the corporate suspects have designated management representatives for legal proceedings, with investigation papers to be submitted to public prosecutors before heading to court.
The companies are being investigated under Articles 98, 99, and 108 of the Environmental Protection and Management Law, which cover deliberate or negligent environmental offences and land burning.
The offences carry penalties of up to 15 years' imprisonment for individuals found liable and fines of up to 15 billion rupiah (RM3.36 million).
"We are proceeding against foreign-affiliated companies or those funded by overseas investment because the alleged offences occurred within the jurisdiction of the Republic of Indonesia," he said.
Asep said police have recommended the revocation of business licences of 23 corporations following findings that included repeated fires within concessions, fires originating on company land, inadequate firefighting facilities, and burned areas exceeding 500 hectares.
He said police had so far received 104 reports involving corporations, covering 29,168.78 hectares of burned land, including 33 reports in West Kalimantan, 20 in South Sumatra, 14 in Central Kalimantan, 13 in South Kalimantan, and seven in East Kalimantan.
For cases involving individuals, police have filed 287 reports covering 5,859.12 hectares of burned land, with 245 people named as suspects.
West Kalimantan recorded the highest number of police reports involving individuals, at 68, followed by Riau (59), Central Kalimantan (43), South Sumatra (42) and East Kalimantan (30).
Asep said that individual cases generally involved deliberate or negligent burning to clear land, with suspects investigated under environmental protection, plantation, and forestry laws.

Title: 5 hours to travel 6km amid Bangsar traffic chaos
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists were caught in severe traffic congestion for hours in Lembah Pantai, Bangsar and Kampung Kerinchi yesterday following heavy rain and fallen trees.
Social media posts showed motorists enduring nearly five hours of slow-moving traffic while travelling to pick up their children from school, despite their homes being just a few kilometres away.
Threads user @lyslysa said she spent nearly five hours travelling from Bangsar South or Kampung Kerinchi to SK Bangsar and back to Pantai Hillpark.
Checks on Google Maps showed that the journey covered an estimated 5km to 6km.
User @ninakhairol also shared a similar experience, saying she was caught in unusually heavy traffic for three hours after picking up her young child from a childcare centre at 5.40pm. She arrived home about three hours later.
Earlier reports said a
fallen tree
along the Kerinchi Link highway, from Bangsar towards Bukit Damansara about 5.10pm yesterday had caused traffic congestion.
Meanwhile, five fallen-tree incidents were reported in Puchong, Selayang and Rawang in Selangor following bad weather in the Klang Valley yesterday evening.

Title: Violent threats from smugglers a part of life for border enforcement personnel
Article:
KOTA BARU: Violent threats from smugglers are part of life for border enforcement personnel.
Smugglers they encounter shout threats at them and occasionally fire shots at them using firearms and air guns.
A former member of a border enforcement unit who only wanted to be identified as Irwandi said he was once shot at with an air gun.
He said he had patrolled the border between Kelantan and Thailand from 2004 till 2022, during which time he had encountered smugglers on several occasions.
The 48-year-old said, during one such encounter, the smugglers fired air guns at his unit, though the shot missed him and his colleagues.
"There were times when we faced threats from smugglers. They would use air guns to intimidate us, and the situation could become dangerous, especially during patrols at night," he said.
Irwandi said smuggling activities along the border involved various contraband, including drugs, firearms and rice.
He said smugglers often operated between 2am and 3am, when most people were asleep, and took advantage of the quiet surroundings to move their goods across the river.
The shallow waters of Sungai Golok also made it easier for smugglers to cross, particularly during the dry season.
"They know the river very well. When the water level drops, crossing becomes much easier, allowing them to move their goods quickly to the other side," he said.
Irwandi said syndicates also had informers who alerted them whenever enforcement personnel were spotted conducting patrols.
He said such warnings made enforcement work more challenging, as smugglers could quickly change their routes or abandon their plans when they learnt of the presence of authorities.
He said tighter security measures and strict adherence to standard operating procedures were crucial whenever threats or attempts to obstruct enforcement operations occurred.
On Tuesday, the New Straits Times had reported that villagers along the Kelantan coast claim they have been
threatened with firearms
by members of human-smuggling syndicates to stop them from exposing illegal activities in their neighbourhoods.
They said the threats had heightened fear among coastal communities, where undocumented migrants were brought ashore almost nightly through rivers, jetties and secluded stretches of beach.
Meanwhile, marine policemen have been ordered to double their operations to curb human-trafficking activities along the Kelantan and Golok rivers as well as waters off Tumpat.
Marine police Region Three commander Assistant Commissioner Mohd Khairuddin Jamal said the directive to strengthen surveillance and enforcement had been issued to all, particularly those operating in Pengkalan Kubor, Tumpat.
He said the number of marine policemen on duty had also been increased in the effort to prevent syndicates from exploiting the country's waterways to smuggle migrants into Malaysia.
"In terms of assets and manpower, operations that were previously conducted twice a week must now be doubled, along with the number of personnel involved," he said when contacted.
Khairuddin said the operations would focus on identified hotspots and routes frequently used by syndicates to transport undocumented migrants.
However, he said the syndicates frequently changed their modus operandi to evade detection.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Community-led innovation for future cities
Article:
LETTER:
Malaysia has made remarkable progress in expanding access to housing, most recently pushing past national targets by delivering more than 511,000 affordable housing units under the Twelfth Malaysia Plan.
Large-scale public housing programmes, urban upgrading efforts and investments in infrastructure have helped improve living conditions for many communities.
Yet new challenges continue to emerge such as rapid urbanisation, with the national urban population now exceeding 75 per cent, changing demographics, rising living costs and climate-related risks are reshaping what Malaysians need from housing today.
As we celebrate this Urban October under the theme "Adequate Housing for All", the question is whether that home is safe, affordable, resilient, well-connected and able to support a decent quality of life.
For Malaysia, as for the world, ensuring adequate housing is central to building inclusive, resilient and sustainable cities. Globally an estimated 2.8 billion people face some form of housing inadequacy, and close to 1.1 billion live in slums and informal settlements.
As climate change intensifies, the need for resilient housing, risk-informed planning and safer urban development becomes increasingly important.
Malaysia is increasingly integrating climate resilience into housing and urban development policies through nature-based solutions, resilient infrastructure and risk-informed planning approaches that seek to protect vulnerable communities while improving urban liveability.
Recognising these challenges, the country recently launched the National Housing Policy 2026-2035, which emphasises housing affordability, a more responsive relationship between housing supply and local demand, stronger housing data systems, integration of housing and transport planning, and the development of a more formal and regulated rental ecosystem.
The policy reflects an important shift: adequate housing is being recognised not only as a matter of construction, but also as a matter of urban liveability, inclusion and long-term resilience.
A decade after world leaders adopted the New Urban Agenda (NUA), the verdict is clear global progress if falling far behind schedule, Member States recommitted to these goals through 2036.
Malaysia's evolving housing agenda positions the country to lead by example to the NUA commitments.
Having hosted the Ninth World Urban Forum (WUF9) and taking on the Presidency of the UN-Habitat Assembly for 2025–2027, Malaysia is no longer following international frameworks, but actively shaping them.
Global goals only matter if they make a difference on your street. That is where UN-Habitat and URBANICE Malaysia focus their work, helping cities and states turn big international commitments into practical local plans.
One way is through Voluntary Local Reviews and Voluntary Subnational Reviews. These are health checks that cities and states carry out on themselves.
They measure how well they are doing on the Sustainable Development Goals, the targets the world has agreed on for ending poverty, protecting the planet and improving lives.
With UN-Habitat's support, Malaysian local authorities have used these reviews to see where they stand, plan with real evidence and bring more voices into decision-making.
URBANICE Malaysia also helps cities learn from one another.
Through the Malaysia Urban Innovation Hub, public forums and hands-on support for local councils, it connects people who are solving similar problems in different places, so a good idea in one town can take root in another.
All of this comes back to a simple point: a home needs a bus stop nearby, clean water, a safe park, jobs within reach and protection from floods, and some of the best ideas come from residents themselves.
At Malaysia Urban Forum 2026, held under the theme "The Future City I Want to Call Home", community members, young people and researchers shared practical ideas for better places to live.
The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) is now funding three community-led pilot projects to put some of those ideas into action.
It is a reminder that people who live in a place usually know best what it needs.
SRINIVASA POPURI
Chief
UN-Habitat Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCA gets Bandar Hilir as third seat to contest in Melaka, ending BN seat dispute
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MCA will contest Bandar Hilir as its third seat in the Melaka election, ending a seat allocation dispute within Barisan Nasional.
Party president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said the agreement followed discussions between BN and Perikatan Nasional, whose leaders agreed to let MCA contest the seat.
"I have even received calls from senior PN leaders expressing their willingness to let MCA contest, as this is a seat we contested previously.
"We are familiar with the area and have a councillor serving there. It is also one of our traditional seats," he told a press conference at parliament today.
MCA will now contest Bandar Hilir alongside Machap Jaya and Klebang. Wee said PN would announce candidates for six seats.
He said BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi handed the appointment letter to MCA's Bandar Hilir candidate, Jasmine Lok Huey Yee, 38, today.
Lok, a Melaka Historic City Council councillor and public relations graduate from Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman, was selected based on her service in the Chinese-majority constituency.
Wee said Bandar Hilir was an additional allocation following MCA's earlier acceptance of two seats and assurances from Zahid that the party would not be sidelined.
"We will pool our strength and carry out all our election work to ensure we can govern. More importantly, we want to secure the support and a fresh mandate from the people of Melaka," he said.
The agreement follows Zahid's assurance that "
all is well
" within BN in a Facebook post yesterday, accompanied by a photograph of him clasping hands with Wee.
The dispute came to the fore when Wee
walked out
during the introduction of BN's candidates at the Melaka International Trade Centre over dissatisfaction with seat negotiations. He said he was defending MCA's dignity and rights as a BN component party.
BN had initially announced it would contest 21 of Melaka's 28 state seats, leaving seven for Pas and its strategic partners.
In the 2021 state election, DAP's Leng Chau Yen won Bandar Hilir with 9,091 votes, or 81.2 per cent, defeating MCA's Lee Kah Sean, who polled 1,313 votes, by a majority of 7,778.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Muhyiddin hopes confidence and supply agreement will last until Parliament is dissolved
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said he hoped the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) signed with the government would remain in place until Parliament is dissolved.
"Because the period is quite long, it gives the government the chance to carry out its agenda, and gives space and opportunity for parties like Bersatu to keep strengthening our position later when facing the election," he told reporters after signing the agreement at Parliament here with several other Bersatu members of Parliament, including Datuk Seri Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Datuk Ali Biju (Saratok), Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Mohd Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai).
Those spotted at the signing included Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin and Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.
Representing the government were deputy prime ministers Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, as well as Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz.
Muhyiddin said the agreement followed the format of the one signed when Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob was prime minister and Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was opposition leader.
"The aim is to create a more stable situation for the country, to continue important matters for the people, mainly in the economy, the cost of living and so on," he said.
He said Bersatu remained in the opposition despite the agreement.
"This agreement does not mean we are free of our responsibility as the opposition," he said.
Under the agreement, the MPs pledged to support the 2027 Budget and institutional reforms, including limiting the prime minister's tenure to a maximum of two terms and separating the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor.
The government, meanwhile, agreed to provide opposition MPs with development allocations equal to those given to government MPs from today and to cover the Bumiputera agenda.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 6 Bersatu MPs, Syed Saddiq sign deal to back Anwar until term ends
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government today signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with six Bersatu MPs and Muar member of Parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman, setting out several conditions in exchange for their support.
The seven MPs want the government to limit the prime minister's tenure and separate the roles of attorney-general and public prosecutor before the current administration's term ends.
They also want to receive the same constituency development allocations as government MPs.
In return, the seven opposition MPs will support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's administration until the end of the parliamentary term, including the 2027 Budget.
The confidence and supply agreement (CSA) was signed by Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Anwar's senior political adviser Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz, and Syed Saddiq.
The six Bersatu MPs involved in the MoU are Muhyiddin (Pagoh), Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Datuk Ali Biju (Saratok), Datuk Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Datuk Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai).
The agreement was also signed by six former Bersatu MPs who were expelled from the party in 2024 after declaring their support for the government.
Anwar previously said allocations could be provided to opposition MPs through a confidence and supply agreement, similar to the agreement reached with the administration of former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob when Anwar was opposition leader.
The government bloc in the Dewan Rakyat currently has 149 MPs, comprising Pakatan Harapan (PH) with 75 seats, Barisan Nasional (30), Gabungan Parti Sarawak (23) and Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (seven).
Three Warisan MPs are also part of the government bloc, alongside one MP each from Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM), Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku (STAR) and Parti Bangsa Malaysia (PBM).
Eight independent MPs also support the government, including six former Bersatu representatives.
The opposition bloc comprises Pas with 43 MPs, Bersatu (19), Wawasan (six) and Muda (one).
Four seats are currently vacant following the resignations of Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli (Pandan), Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad (Setiawangsa), Wong Chen (Subang) and Lee Chean Chung (Petaling Jaya).
With 218 serving MPs at present, a simple majority requires the support of at least 110 MPs, while a two-thirds majority requires 146.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hong Kong leader apologises for deadly Tai Po fire, pledges reforms
Article:
HONG KONG: Hong Kong leader John Lee apologised on Thursday for the deadly blaze that killed 168 people in the city last November, promising swift but extensive reforms to its building industry and regulatory system.
Lee was speaking shortly before he released a more than 1,000-page report by the judge-led panel that detailed wide-ranging governance and supervisory failings in Hong Kong's building-renovation system.
Lee also announced the resignation of Hong Kong's Housing Secretary Winnie Ho, echoing the report by saying that four government bodies bore partial responsibility for a blaze that the report said was most likely started by a "glowing source...likely a cigarette."
"As chief executive and head of the government, I am deeply saddened," Lee said in his opening remarks.
"On behalf of the SAR government, I offer my apologies to the victims and the public at large."
Ho was the first official to resign over the inferno. The Hong Kong government has set up an independent team to investigate which officials should be held accountable and to outline disciplinary actions.
Lee said Hong Kong's Chief Secretary Eric Chan will now head a steering committee to oversee reforms advocated in the report, which will include laws to criminalise bid-rigging across the construction industry with fines of up to HK$10 million and 10 years' imprisonment.
The committee report said contractor Prestige Construction & Engineering Co Ltd and project consultant Will Power Architects Co Ltd should bear primary responsibility.
[[nid:1566263]]
At least 25 criminal charges related to the Wang Fuk Court fire have been made against Prestige, Will Power and seven individuals, including manslaughter, conspiracy to defraud, money laundering and tax evasion.
But the report also went further, outlining widespread unlawful and dubious construction practices as a "corrupt eco-system."
The rigging of bids involved many different parties, some linked to triad organised crime gangs, it said.
"The fire has been put out, but the reform has only just begun," the report stated.
"The Committee finds that no Government department took effective ownership of various fire safety issues and complaints about fire hazards fell into a vacuum," the report stated.
The blaze ripped through seven 31-storey tower blocks at the Wang Fuk Court residential complex, which was undergoing renovation work in the northern Tai Po district.
It was the deadliest in the city since 1948.  Thousands of residents were displaced after their homes became uninhabitable.
The committee held 30 hearings this year with 80 witnesses, including residents, property management and renovation personnel, engineering and fire experts, government officials and regulators.
It evaluated more than one million files and submissions as it investigated the cause of the fire and reviewed oversight of building renovations.

Title: Never exploit royal ties and influence for profit - Sultan Nazrin
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR: The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, has warned members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court against misusing the Ruler's name, royal influence and their titles for personal gain.
His Royal Highness cautioned against exploiting such privileges for financial profit or business opportunities.
He also urged them not to allow themselves to be used to assist parties in an improper or questionable manner, or to exert undue pressure on anyone.
"Shun corruption, the abuse of power and any conduct that might give rise to suspicion or tarnish the reputation of the throne and the Royal Court.
"Never allow your position to become a means of seeking special privileges, accumulating personal wealth or interfering in matters beyond the scope of your responsibilities," he decreed at the 175th Meeting of Dewan Negara Perak at Istana Iskandariah here today.
Sultan Nazrin also urged members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court to remain vigilant and exercise sound judgement in communications, particularly when using social media channels and platforms.
"...exercise care and discretion in both word and deed. Matters entrusted to you in confidence must be safeguarded. Information whose accuracy has yet to be established must not be circulated.
"Opinions should be expressed with due propriety, without giving rise to slander or discord. In today's world, a single remark or recording shared on social media can give rise to many different interpretations," he said.
His Royal Highness also called on them to avoid disputes, power struggles and factionalism while maintaining close ties with the people.
He said public grievances must be heard and addressed, particularly those involving vulnerable groups such as senior citizens, persons with disabilities, orphans, low-income families and marginalised communities.
"Maintain good relations with people from every walk of life. Our State is home to people of diverse ethnicities, religions and backgrounds. Respect this diversity and work towards strengthening unity, in accordance with the Constitution and the law," he said.
Sultan Nazrin said members of Dewan Negara Perak and royal dignitaries must understand the role of the monarchy within the framework of a constitutional monarchy.
"Respect the prescribed limits of authority and responsibility. Work professionally with the government and state institutions, without interfering in administrative affairs or using your position to advance partisan political interests," he said.
The Sultan also encouraged them to continuously broaden their knowledge and improve their ways of working, understand societal changes, and make prudent use of technology.
The Sultan further stressed that every palace dignitary must set an example for their families, officers, staff and the wider community.
"Show that those who are close to the Ruler are equally committed to their responsibilities, and that those who are accorded honour also know how to honour others," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Syed Saddiq: CSA must ensure fair funding, curb PM's powers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Muar member of Parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman said the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) must deliver genuine reforms before the next general election.
He said the reforms would curb the prime minister's powers and ensure fair constituency funding, with legislation needed to bind future administrations.
"Sometimes people focus too much on allocations. But allocations without legislation will not bring about major change.
"I think this is genuine progress. My hope is that it can be done as soon as possible," he told reporters after the signing of the CSA at Parliament today.
Earlier, six Bersatu MPs led by party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and seven other opposition MPs signed the CSA. Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin was also seen at the signing.
A live video on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's Facebook page showed Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Anwar's senior political adviser, Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz, at the signing.
The agreement provides for equal constituency funding, calls for limits on the prime minister's tenure and the separation of the attorney-general and public prosecutor's roles before the administration's term ends.
In return, the MPs pledged to support Anwar's administration until the end of the parliamentary term and back the 2027 Budget.
Syed Saddiq said Muda supported the agreement's three reform priorities.
"This is not about (Prime Minister) Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim alone. I hope it will continue to apply to future prime ministers," he said.
On constituency funding, Syed Saddiq said the agreement stipulated equal allocations for government and opposition MPs covered by the arrangement, although no specific amount had been announced.
He said it also marked the start of a process to legislate fair allocations, preventing funding from being granted to political allies while being withheld from opponents.
"I think it is a good beginning, and I hope this will be extended to all other opposition MPs. I have also told government representatives: it should not stop at us."
Syed Saddiq said he had held eight rounds of negotiations over two-and-a-half years and was pleased that the discussions had yielded results.
"My hope, as an opposition MP, and I remain an opposition MP, is that we can find common ground so that allocations can be distributed fairly and equitably to everyone," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High Court upholds 17-year jail sentence for man in gang rape case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has upheld a 17-year jail sentence imposed on a man who took turns with two others to rape their friend's 26-year-old sister-in-law in 2023.
Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin dismissed 31-year-old Nik Khaira Hafizi Mat Zaid's appeal against the sentence imposed by the Sessions Court on June 16, 2024.
In her grounds of judgment, Noor Ruwena said there was no error of fact or law warranting appellate intervention.
She ruled that the punishment was appropriate given the gravity of the offence and the trauma suffered by the victim.
The rape took place at 3.30am on Aug 30, 2023, when four men, including the victim's brother in-law, entered her room while she was asleep.
They restrained her by binding her hands with cellophane tape and stuffed a laundry bag into her mouth to prevent her from screaming.
Nik Khaira and two others took turns to rape the victim while the fourth man helped restrain her and watched the assault.
She tried to kick a window to attract help but was unable to free herself. After the men left, she called 999.
Nik Khaira was charged alongside three men, one of whom was the victim's brother-in-law, who enabled the attack by allowing the other men into the house.
They pleaded guilty after the prosecution had called four witnesses, including the victim.
The Sessions Court sentenced Nik Khaira and two others to 17 years' jail while the fourth man received 14 years.
In the appeal, the National Legal Aid Foundation said the sentencing should consider rehabilitation and a chance to turn over a new leaf.
Deputy public prosecutor Faizal @ Amrin Noor Hadi said the jail term was just.
Noor Ruwena said the aggravating circumstances included the betrayal of trust by the victim's brother-in-law, who had facilitated the crime, and the collective actions of the four men in carrying out the assault.
She rejected the argument that Nik Khaira's status as a first time offender warranted a greater reduction.
"He did not come across (to me) as an immature young offender who may not know the extent of seriousness of the crime," she said.
She borrowed the words of a High Court judge who had said if one was brave enough to tempt fate and get caught, he must be brave enough to face consequences of his act.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian family robbed of 11 bags during Italy trip
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian family travelling in Italy was left distressed after 11 pieces of luggage were allegedly stolen from their car while they stopped for a meal in Pisa.
The incident was shared by Threads user njlaimn, who said a friend and their family were affected while travelling from Pisa to Milan.
The family managed to track their missing iPad to an area believed to be a gypsy camp.
The incident also raised safety concerns, with the family reportedly disappointed by the authorities' response, which fell short of their expectations.
The post drew various reactions from netizens, with some sharing similar experiences and warning travellers against leaving luggage unattended in vehicles.
One commenter advised travellers to head directly from their hotels or accommodation to the airport without making unnecessary stops.
"My advice is to travel directly from your hotel or accommodation to the airport without stopping at other unnecessary places. Never leave luggage unattended in a parked car, even if it is locked," the commenter said.
Another user, farhayayakob, warned travellers against using expensive luggage brands and leaving their bags in a car in a public area.
Another commenter, fakamal, said travellers should make arrangements to transport their luggage to their accommodation before going out to explore.
"Leaving bags like that in a car is practically inviting thieves in Italy. Make the effort to send your luggage to your accommodation first, then go out sightseeing," the user wrote.
Other netizens expressed sympathy for the family and hoped their difficulties would be eased and that they would return home safely.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man found dead in storeroom
Article:
LAWAS: A 35-year-old man was found lying dead in a storeroom at a government agency here yesterday.
He was found by a colleague at 9.05am before other colleagues were alerted and he was taken to Lawas Hospital for treatment.
Lawas district police chief Deputy Superintendent Liong Tindan said the man was pronounced dead by medical personnel who examined him.
"At the time of the incident, the victim was reportedly tidying up the storeroom while his colleagues were outside.
"Initial investigations at the scene found no elements of crime involving the victim," he said.
Liong said police received a report on the incident at 12.03pm the same day.
The case has been classified as sudden death (SDR).
He urged anyone with information on the incident to assist investigations by contacting the authorities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Philippine minister says Asean does not share China's view on defence forum
Article:
CEBU: The Philippine defence minister said on Thursday that Asean countries do not share the view of China's defence ministry on the its participation in a regional defence forum, adding that no country has the right to characterise Asean processes.
How Asean countries are heard is for Asean to determine, and the important fact is China was able to articulate their position, Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said,
Beijing, however, accused Manila of "erecting multiple obstacles" for its attendance at an Asean meeting in the Philippines this week, where China will be represented by an embassy attache.
"The Philippine side has allowed certain politicians to use public office for private ends and erected multiple obstacles to obstruct China's participation in the Asean Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus," a spokesperson for the Chinese defence ministry told a news conference.
In another development, the Philippines, Japan, Australia and the United States, a grouping known as the Squad, have affirmed a collective desire to enhance their cooperation toward a safer and more prosperous Indo-Pacific, the Philippine defence minister said.

Title: Strengthening national resilience through environmental security
Article:
MALAYSIA'S environmental approach rests on the National Policy on the Environment (DASN), which promotes sustainable resource use and the Environmental Quality Act 1974 (EQA), providing a legal basis for pollution control.
Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 13, 14 and 15 address climate action, marine ecosystems and life on land. Malaysia also participates in the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP), recognising that some environmental risks cannot be managed within national borders alone.
The challenge is turning these commitments into practical protection for communities and essential services. The priority is to make existing arrangements work together, rather than assume that additional policies or institutions will solve the problem.
The November 2020 Sungai Selangor pollution incident shows how an environmental problem can quickly affect daily life when four water treatment plants temporarily stopped operating, disrupting supplies in parts of the Klang Valley.
Although authorities responded, the interruption shows why shared information, clear responsibilities and early preventive measures matter.
Protecting a water source is also about maintaining the service it provides.
Some threats extend beyond Malaysia's control. Transboundary haze can affect health, schools and economic activity even when fires occur outside the country.
AATHP provides a basis for cooperation, while the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) shares hotspot and weather assessments.
Regional progress therefore depends on countries sharing information promptly, examining conditions on the ground and acting on common assessments within their own legal powers.
Environmental monitoring also offers an opportunity to act earlier. Malaysia and Asean already use monitoring networks, satellites and location-based information.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) could help connect these sources, identify unusual patterns and support forecasts.
However, an alert is useful only if its reliability can be checked and someone has the authority to respond. Poor data, false warnings and cybersecurity risks can weaken confidence.
AI should assist experienced officials, not replace their judgement or legal responsibilities.
Across these examples, the central issue is the link between knowledge and action.
Policies set priorities, agencies protect services, regional partners share information and monitoring tools identify risks.
National resilience improves when these functions support timely, coordinated decisions rather than operate separately.
To address these weaknesses, we should establish a Malaysia Environmental Security Resilience Framework (MESRF).
It rests on Policy and SDG Integration, Governance and Regional Cooperation, and AI-enabled Environmental Intelligence.
Its guiding principle is to connect existing institutions before creating new ones.
Four initiatives would put the framework into practice.
First, develop a set of Environmental Security Indicators to show where environmental pressures threaten people and essential services.
Second, federal and state agencies should agree on practical procedures for sharing risk information, checking warnings and deciding who should act.
Third, strengthen the operational value of Asean cooperation by exchanging timely information, conducting joint assessments where appropriate and reviewing responses after regional warnings.
Fourth, an AI-Enabled National Environmental Intelligence Platform (AI-NEIP) could be explored as a decision-support tool connecting environmental, satellite and geospatial data.
Environmental security is ultimately about keeping communities and essential services functioning when environmental conditions deteriorate.
Malaysia already has sound policies, laws, regional partnerships and monitoring capabilities. Their value depends on how effectively information moves between institutions and leads to action.
Success should be judged by earlier credible warnings, better coordinated prevention and fewer avoidable interruptions to essential services.
Stronger national resilience begins with making existing capabilities work together.
* The writer is Assistant Commissioner of Police, Royal Malaysian Police and currently attending the National Resilience College at the National Centre for Defence Studies (PUSPAHANAS), Putrajaya
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hello Kitty firm scraps Japan TV tie-up after 'anti-China' backlash
Article:
BEIJING: Sanrio, the Japanese company that owns the popular Hello Kitty character, apologised Thursday over its tie-up with a TV spy drama criticised as anti-China, cancelling a merchandise collaboration with the show.
It comes after Chinese sponsors dropped football superstar Kylian Mbappe over comments calling communist leader Mao Zedong a "dictator", which the Real Madrid forward later apologised for.
"We have recently received feedback from various quarters regarding the collaborative merchandise with the Japanese television drama VIVANT," Sanrio's Chinese unit said on social media platform Weibo.
"We sincerely apologise for any concern this may have caused," the post said.
The project "contains expressions that are inconsistent with the Sanrio Group's corporate philosophy", it said.
Sanrio said it had "decided to cease this collaboration, as well as all subsequent projects and promotional campaigns."
In one episode of the TV drama, a Chinese-affiliated organisation had been depicted torturing a member of the Japanese military's unofficial spy unit.
Chinese state media outlet The Global Times had called the show "notorious for smearing China", saying it had sparked shock and fierce backlash on social media."
The series reflects the "anti-China narrative of the current conservative Japanese right-wing administration, catering to the trend of right-wing extremism in Japanese society", it said.
Contacted by AFP, private broadcaster TBS, which created the drama Vivant, could not immediately comment.
The network's president told Japanese media that the drama is "a fictional entertainment work" and that TBS "does not in any way take a position that foments conflict between nations or condones the use of force or violence."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Parkland wins approval for Main Market listing, to issue 621.54mil new shares
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Property developer Parkland Bhd has received approval from the Securities Commission (SC) for its initial public offering (IPO) and proposed listing on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia.
The IPO will comprise 621.54 million shares, representing 26.3 per cent of the group's enlarged issued share capital of 2.36 billion shares upon listing.
It will comprise a public issue of 468.14 million new shares and an offer for sale of 153.40 million existing shares.
Of the total IPO shares, 550.74 million will be made available to institutional and selected investors, as well as Bumiputera investors approved by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry.
The remaining 70.80 million shares will be offered to the public through balloting, as well as eligible employees and persons who have contributed to the group's success.
Proceeds from the public issue will be used mainly to acquire landbanks and fund working capital for the group's developments.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd is the principal adviser for the IPO and, together with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, will act as joint placement agent and joint underwriter.
Parkland, which develops integrated townships and residential properties in Johor, Melaka and Selangor, has a planned development pipeline worth RM5.05 billion as at May 25, 2026.
About 75.5 per cent of the pipeline is located in Johor.
With 18 years of experience in construction and property development, Parkland has launched integrated townships and standalone property projects with a total gross development value (GDV) of RM7.4 billion across the launched phases.
Its ongoing developments include the Taman Kluang Perdana, Taman Bukit Perdana, Taman Parkland and Bandar Layangkasa townships, as well as Parkland by The River in Johor.
In Melaka, its projects include the Bandar Botani Parkland township and Parkland Avenue by The Sea development.
Parkland has also ventured into renewable energy through a joint venture with Xinyi Power Station Development (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Hong Kong-listed Xinyi Energy Holdings Ltd.
The joint venture has secured the development of a 99.99-megawatt large-scale solar plant in Tangkak, Johor, which is expected to begin commercial operations in the first quarter of 2027.
Group managing director Datuk Tan See Sen said the SC's approval marks a significant milestone in Parkland's journey towards listing on the Main market.
"The proposed IPO will provide us with a stronger platform to accelerate our development plans, expand our land bank and further strengthen our position in the property development industry.
"Moving forward, we remain committed to leveraging our established presence in Johor, Melaka and Selangor while pursuing strategic opportunities that support the group's long-term growth," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thailand targets US$1bil in assets as alleged scam suspects flee
Article:
BANGKOK: Thai authorities have vowed to seize more than US$1 billion in assets from a group accused of laundering proceeds from Southeast Asia-based scam syndicates.
A criminal court issued arrest warrants Tuesday for the alleged ring leader, South African Ben Smith, his Thai wife Cattaliya Beevor, Cambodian businessman Yim Leak and four others, police said.
Media reports have previously linked Smith, also known as Benjamin Mauerberger, to transnational scam operations in Cambodia, part of a multibillion-dollar illicit industry that has ballooned in the region.
Yim Leak, who denies the charge, belongs to an elite political family and is the brother of a senior Cambodian police official.
Smith, Cattaliya, Yim Leak and three others have fled Thailand, the country's Securities and Exchange Commission said in a statement.
Thai anti-money laundering officials and securities regulators told reporters Tuesday that illicit proceeds from criminal enterprises were moved by the group through overseas financial firms before being traded for stocks on the Thai stock exchange.
The Anti-Money Laundering Office (AMLO) will seize assets, including shares worth more than 14 billion baht, and real estate, cash and vehicles valued at 21 billion baht, totalling more than US$1 billion, police said in a statement.
The seizures included shares in major Thai firms, including Bangchak, one of the country's biggest oil refiners, according to AMLO deputy head Kamonsit Wongbutnoi.
Bangchak said in a statement that the asset seizures concerned individual investors and business operations were unaffected.
Confiscated assets would go towards compensating victims of online scams, Kamonsit told reporters.
The group of seven were charged with conspiracy to launder money and acting as a criminal organisation, police said.
Lanny Davis, a spokesman for Yim Leak, said the accusations against the Cambodian businessman were "100 per cent false."
"There isn't a shred of truth that he's ever been involved in scam operations in Thailand, in Cambodia or anywhere else," Davis told AFP.
He said Yim Leak denied the charge and challenged the Thai government to provide "any evidence of his knowledge or involvement" in scam operations.
An Oct 8 statement issued by Yim Leak's lawyers accused Thai officials of conducting a trial by media against him before he was charged.
It said Thailand froze more than US$600 million in assets, including his family's, without a hearing.
A lawyer for Smith, Witoon Kengngan, declined to comment on Wednesday.
In February, Thai authorities ordered the seizure of assets worth more than US$410 million from Smith and other individuals accused of fraud.
Thai opposition lawmaker Rangsiman Rome, who is being sued by Smith for defamation over comments he made about scams, told AFP on Wednesday the fresh seizures and arrest warrants were "a positive development... even if it's taken a while."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Spain declares three days of mourning after train crash kills 68, injures over 100
Article:
URDA: Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday after its second high-speed rail collision this year killed 68 people and injured scores, with relatives desperately seeking news about their loved ones.
One of Europe's deadliest train disasters this century has raised fresh questions about safety on Spain's rail network after the transport minister reported an "error" and "inexplicable circumstances" that led to the crash.
The collision happened in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha on Wednesday morning when a service by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo.
Emergency services combed through the wreckage at night to find further victims on the key line linking Madrid with the southern city of Seville, hoisting pieces of mangled metal with cranes, AFP reporters saw.
At daybreak, police drones were once again flying over the crash site a few kilometres from the small village of Urda
Josimar Medina, a 31-year-old Peruvian who was holidaying in Spain with his girlfriend, said he was sleeping on the Renfe train when "I woke up and I was in the air."
Pablo Mejia, 42, escaped with injuries to his head, telling AFP that a last-minute change of seat saved his life.
Wearing a bloodstained grey jumper and holding his tattered suitcase, he recounted "a very strong hit... a lot of people on the floor, on top of each other, seats ripped out, suitcases, a lot of chaos."
"I think I've been born again," he said.
- 'FINAL MOMENT' -
A school in Urda, around 130km south of Madrid, is being used to allow relatives to enquire about their loved ones.
Teams of Red Cross workers offered support to groups of people who arrived, some of them in tears, amid crowds of police and journalists from around the world.
Red Cross psychologist Carmen Garcia said "long and hard hours" were in store because "every person will manage it in their own way.
"We have people who are in shock, who haven't taken on board what has happened, angry people, sad, worried people. The grieving will be complicated," Garcia said.
The Civil Guard has set up four offices in the cities of Madrid, Toledo, Cordoba and Seville to enable relatives of the victims to provide DNA samples and help identify the missing.
Blood donation points have also been set up in Castilla-La Mancha and Madrid.
Jose Miguel Fernandez, a parish priest in Urda, joined the emergency services in offering support to the victims' families.
"It is important for relatives to find their loved ones, even if they have died, because the grieving process is quicker when you have been able to say goodbye at that final moment," he told radio Onda Cero.
- SAFETY QUESTIONS -
Flags flew at half-mast on public buildings as the country observed a day of mourning, with official ceremonies and public events cancelled or scaled back as a mark of respect for the victims.
Transport Minister Oscar Puente said on Wednesday that an automatic control system went down on 69km of track, causing all trains there to be stopped.
But the control centre decided to "resume traffic in circumstances that, from our point of view, are inexplicable," Puente said, with the Renfe train travelling 25km before striking the Iryo.
The control centre "had more than enough time to verify the error, and they did not fix it", he added.
In January, two high-speed trains collided in the southern region of Andalusia after one of them derailed and crossed onto the adjacent track, killing 46 people.
The investigation into that accident is ongoing, but the left-wing government faced heavy criticism over its management of Spain's railways.
The latest disaster comes one month before Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez seeks to overturn unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership in an early general election on Nov 29.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US fires top army general in latest ouster: Media
Article:
WASHINGTON: The United States has fired its top military planner, The Atlantic reported Wednesday, in a surprise shake-up as President Donald Trump appears to be preparing to resume large-scale strikes against Iran.
Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed this week from his role as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the magazine reported, citing unidentified defence department officials.
Sylvia's ouster would be the latest in a series of high-profile departures from the military since Trump returned to power a year ago.
Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth said last month that the United States has slashed the number of its generals and admirals by 20 per cent, in a move he said is aimed at "accountability."
He suggested the cuts targeted officers who failed to get on board with his efforts to ensure the military is focused on war-fighting rather than the "woke" policies of previous administrations, describing the reductions as an "accomplishment."
No reason was given for Sylvia's departure and no replacement has been named, The Atlantic said.
AFP has contacted the Pentagon for comment.
The reported sacking comes as Trump is widely considered to be weighing fresh strikes against Iran after the US midterm elections on Nov 3.
"We may do another little Epic Fury," Trump said last week, referring to US-Israeli attacks on Teheran in February that triggered the war.
He did not give any indication on timing.
Neither the United States nor Iran has engaged in major attacks on land-based targets since early September, settling instead into a pattern of strikes on commercial ships.
Sylvia's previous roles included leading the 101st Airborne Division – the US army's air assault division – and heading a unit in Iraq.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MOH to conduct special recruitment for 750 permanent medical officer posts in Sabah, Sarawak
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 29 — The Health Ministry (MOH) will conduct a special recruitment exercise to fill 750 permanent Medical Officer Grade UD10 vacancies in Sabah and Sarawak, with applications open from November 9 to 15.
MOH said the recruitment is open to all contract-appointed medical officers who began their housemanship training from Series 1/2016 on December 5, 2016, to Series 6/2024 on October 14, 2024, including those whose service contracts had expired.
“To be eligible, candidates must have successfully completed their housemanship training and obtained full registration with the Malaysian Medical Council by the closing date of the application advertisement at the latest,” MOH said in a statement today.
The ministry said eligible and interested officers could submit their applications through the Public Service Commission’s SPA9 system when the recruitment advertisement opened.
“For officers who are successful in securing permanent appointments, the proposed reporting date is February 15, 2027,” the statement said.
The ministry said the recruitment exercise was part of the Madani Government’s commitment to making permanent appointments for more than 9,000 medical officers, as announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling Budget 2027.
“This proactive measure is also designed to narrow the staffing gap and ensure that the retention of the medical workforce in Sabah and Sarawak remains at an optimal level,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: Former Pahang water firm procurement manager begins three-year jail term after losing bribery appeal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 29 — The Court of Appeal today upheld the three-year jail sentence and RM239,500 fine imposed on a former procurement manager of Pengurusan Air Pahang Berhad after dismissing his appeal to set aside his conviction on 22 charges of receiving RM44,700 in bribes.
A three-member panel led by Justice Datuk Noorin Badaruddin ruled that Sani Khan Ali Khan had failed to show any error of law or material fact in the High Court decision that convicted him on all the charges.
On January 26, the Kuantan High Court set aside a Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged him of all the charges.
The Court of Appeal panel, which also comprised Justices Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, ordered him to begin serving his sentence today.
Sani Khan, 51, had previously been granted a stay of execution and released on RM20,000 bail with one surety pending the outcome of this appeal.
In today’s proceedings, Justice Noorin said the High Court’s intervention was justified and that it had made no material error in setting aside the Sessions Court decision that had acquitted and discharged Sani Khan.
“The statutory presumption under Section 50(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 applies,” she said.
She said banking records proved that the money had been received into the appellant’s bank account, and that his claim that the payments were house rental was unconvincing.
Justice Noorin said that although the appellant relied on tenancy agreements and bank transactions labelled as house rent, the court found that the documents did not prove the payments were genuine rent.
She added that the appellant had also failed to show that the alleged defects in the charges had caused him to misunderstand the case or suffer material prejudice in preparing his defence.
Justice Noorin said the evidence was assessed cumulatively, with the banking records, witness testimony, tenancy documents and surrounding circumstances weighed together for each charge. The court found no material error warranting the overturning of any of the 22 convictions.
On December 26, 2024, the Sessions Court ruled that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt, and acquitted and discharged Sani Khan on all the charges.
However, the High Court allowed the prosecution’s appeal to set aside his acquittal and found him guilty on all 22 charges.
The High Court imposed three years’ jail for each charge and ordered Sani Khan to pay a RM239,500 fine, or 12 months’ jail in default. The sentences were ordered to run concurrently.
At the Court of Appeal today, MACC deputy public prosecutors Law Chin How, Haresh Prakash Somiah and Hazel Tan Jia Qi appeared for the prosecution.
Sani Khan was represented by lawyers Mohd Baharuddin Ahmad Kassim, Datuk Mohd Najid Husain and Nornajihah Ahmad Nadjemudin. — Bernama

Title: Menara Tun Perak, formerly Menara Maybank, on offer for full or partial sale
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Menara Tun Perak, the iconic Kuala Lumpur skyscraper formerly known as Menara Maybank, has reportedly been put up for sale after serving as the banking giant’s headquarters for nearly four decades.
According to a sponsored announcement published by property news website
Mingtiandi
, investors are being offered the opportunity to acquire either a partial or full interest in the building, although no asking price was disclosed.
Standing 244 metres tall along Jalan Tun Perak, the building was completed in 1988 and remains one of the capital’s most recognisable landmarks.
The proposed sale comes months after Maybank relocated its headquarters to Merdeka 118 on May 6, ending its longstanding use of the tower as its head office.
On July 28, Maybank announced that its new headquarters would be renamed Menara Merdeka Maybank, while its former headquarters would take the name Menara Tun Perak.
Property consultancy firms Knight Frank Malaysia and CBRE|WTW have reportedly been jointly appointed to advise on the proposed sale.
The building’s location near Chinatown, Central Market, Dataran Merdeka and several public transport stations is being promoted as a key attraction for potential investors.
According to the announcement, interested buyers could retain the property for commercial use, upgrade the existing building or explore converting it into a hotel, serviced accommodation or mixed-use development, subject to feasibility studies and regulatory approvals.
Knight Frank Malaysia head of capital markets James Buckley said properties of such prominence in Kuala Lumpur's historic commercial district were seldom offered to investors.
“Landmark assets of this nature, particularly those located within the city’s historic core, are rarely made available for investment,” he said.
CBRE|WTW director Marcus Yeo said the building's location and potential for alternative uses could appeal to investors amid the continued redevelopment of Kuala Lumpur's city centre.

Title: Muhyiddin: CSA has nothing to do with possible Bersatu-PH pact for Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) signed with the federal government today has nothing to do with a possible electoral pact with Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the Melaka polls,
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT) reported.
“That is a separate question. That has nothing to do with (the agreement) here,” he was quoted as telling reporters after the signing at Parliament.
According to the news portal, Muhyiddin was responding to a question on whether Bersatu would now form an electoral pact with PH in Melaka.
FMT reported that speculation of a tie-up emerged after leaders from both sides attended a closed-door dinner in Melaka on September 28, though the matter has faced pushback within PH.
Muhyiddin also said the CSA was separate from a similar agreement being sought between Bersatu and the PH-led Selangor government, the report said.
“That is another matter. This agreement is between the federal government, represented by the prime minister, and MPs representing my party and the other parties involved,” he said.
According to FMT, the CSA involved six Bersatu MPs and Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman. The MPs are seeking a limit on the prime minister’s tenure and the separation of the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor before the end of the government’s term.
They also want the same constituency development allocations that government backbenchers currently receive.
In return, the seven opposition MPs will support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s administration until the end of the parliamentary term, as well as Budget 2027, the news portal reported.
The six Bersatu MPs who signed are Muhyiddin (Pagoh), Datuk Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Ali Biju (Saratok), Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai).
FMT reported that six former Bersatu MPs, who were sacked in 2024 for declaring support for the government, also signed the deal. Muhyiddin said their signing was merely a formality as they had already expressed support for the prime minister.
He said Bersatu would remain in the opposition and continue to provide checks and balances despite the agreement.
Muhyiddin added that the CSA is expected to remain in force until Parliament is dissolved, but could be terminated if either side failed to honour its commitments.
Separately, Syed Saddiq told FMT the CSA must lead to legislation guaranteeing fair and equal constituency allocations for all MPs, rather than benefiting only those who signed it.
He said the agreement specified that allocations for MPs on both sides must be equal, although the exact amounts had not been disclosed.

Title: Kedah police arrest man over viral video of reckless driving in ‘Bomba’ MPV
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 29 — Police have arrested a 35-year-old man over a viral video showing him allegedly driving recklessly in a red multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) bearing the word ‘Bomba’.
Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said investigations found that the man had been diagnosed with bipolar disorder nine years ago but was believed to have discontinued treatment about two years ago.
“Police received a report on Tuesday following the video’s circulation. The man was arrested in Bandar Puteri Jaya, where the vehicle and several other items were seized,” he told reporters at the Kuala Muda district police headquarters here today.
Hanyan said the man owned the MPV, held a valid driving licence and had no previous criminal record. His urine screening test was negative.
The case is being investigated under Section 170 of the Penal Code for impersonating a public servant and Section 42 of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless and dangerous driving.
The man was remanded for one day before being admitted to Sungai Petani Hospital for treatment and further monitoring.
Hanyan urged families to ensure members with a history of psychiatric treatment attend scheduled follow-up appointments.
The viral video showed the man driving recklessly in the red MPV marked ‘Bomba’ and berating motorists who did not give way to him. — Bernama

Title: Transport minister takes first AirBorneo flight, stresses need for reliable air links to remote communities
Article:
MIRI, Oct 29 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke took his first flight with AirBorneo on a trip from Miri to Limbang, highlighting the importance of rural air connectivity for communities in Sarawak and Sabah.
In a Facebook post on Wednesday, Loke shared photographs of himself on the tarmac with one of the airline’s turboprop aircraft before travelling to Limbang to officiate a local government function.
“Reliable air connectivity is an absolute lifeline for communities in the interior of Sarawak and Sabah.
“Seeing AirBorneo successfully operate these essential routes reinforces our shared commitment to leaving no community isolated,” he said in the post.
Loke said the ministry would continue to support the development of regional aviation to ensure rural communities remained accessible.
AirBorneo operates the Rural Air Services (RAS) in Sarawak and Sabah, connecting remote settlements such as Bario and Long Lellang, where road access is limited or unavailable.
These flights provide an essential transport link for residents, particularly in medical emergencies and for the delivery of essential goods.
The airline’s fleet includes ATR 72 turboprop aircraft serving main routes linking Miri, Kuching and Kota Kinabalu, as well as DHC-6 Twin Otters designed for short take-off and landing at remote airstrips that cannot accommodate larger aircraft.
Beyond its Rural Air Services, AirBorneo also operates scheduled domestic and international passenger flights.
