In July 2026, the airline expanded into jet operations, introducing commercial flights from Kuching to destinations including Kuala Lumpur and Singapore. — The Borneo Post

Title: Govt deputy ministers welcome Bersatu CSA, say pact shows Madani respects all elected reps
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Madani government respects all elected representatives regardless of their party’s size or political strength, Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said today, following Bersatu’s signing of a confidence and supply agreement (CSA) with the government.
The Segamat MP said that despite having a two-thirds majority in Parliament, the government should still engage with the opposition rather than assume it can act unilaterally.
“Unlike some coalitions that prioritise political grandstanding over genuine democratic bargaining, the Madani government has demonstrated that negotiations can be conducted with dignity, mutual respect and a firm commitment to democratic principles,” he said.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said there was precedent for such an agreement, which could provide stability for the passage and implementation of the Budget.
“The priority must be to ensure that the rakyat receive tangible benefits, including fair access to constituency development resources.
“This support should come with a clear commitment to push for positive institutional reforms and hold the government accountable for delivering them,” the Kulai MP said.
Bersatu signed the CSA at Parliament today, pledging its support for the Supply Bill 2027, or Budget 2027,
The Star
reported.
Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin told reporters that, in return, the government had agreed to give the party’s MPs the same constituency development allocations as government MPs.
He said the agreement also covered institutional reforms, including proposals to limit the prime minister’s tenure to two terms and to separate the powers of the Attorney General.
Muhyiddin stressed that Bersatu remained in the opposition and would continue to provide checks and balances.
Muda’s Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman was also involved in the signing, which was facilitated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.

Title: Amir Hamzah: Malaysia confident of exceeding 5pc GDP growth in 2026 as strong economy benefits the people
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The government is confident that economic growth will exceed 5.0 per cent this year, marking the third consecutive year of growth above 5.0 per cent under the Madani Government, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
“Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew by 6.0 per cent in the second quarter of 2026. With overall GDP growth for 2026 projected at between 4.8 and 5.3 per cent, the government is confident that growth will exceed 5.0 per cent this year,” he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage for the Ministry of Finance (MoF) in the Dewan Rakyat today.
In its recent Preliminary Estimates of GDP report, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) estimated that the Malaysian economy expanded by 5.3 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, following growth of 6.0 per cent in the preceding quarter.
DOSM said the growth was supported by positive performances across all economic sectors, except mining and quarrying, which recorded a contraction.
“Cumulatively, for the first three quarters of 2026, the Malaysian economy registered growth of 5.5 per cent, higher than the 4.8 per cent recorded in the corresponding period of 2025,” DOSM said.
Amir Hamzah said growth in 2027 is projected to be between 4.2 and 5.2 per cent.
The unemployment rate remained low at 2.9 per cent in August. The value of approved investments and trade reached the highest levels in history.
“The ringgit remains resilient. The country’s competitiveness ranking also improved significantly, rising from 34th in 2024 to 15th spot in just two years. These achievements show that the national economy is on the right track, with strong fundamentals despite global uncertainties.
“We are mobilising the capabilities and contributions of all parties to advance the nation-building agenda anchored in the Madani Economy framework.”
The aim is to develop high-value economic sectors and master the latest technologies to create better jobs and improve the people’s well-being, he said.
“Additionally, we want the country to remain grounded in good governance, strong unity among its people, and the continued preservation of its national treasures and heritage.” — Bernama

Title: MCMC reviewing need for further regulations on online games, including Roblox, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is reviewing the need for further regulatory measures on online gaming platforms, including Roblox, to enhance child protection against digital safety risks.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC, together with the Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF), is currently studying online gaming trends and associated risks, including user-to-user interactions, in-game content, and protective safeguards implemented by platform providers.
He said the study also takes into account international practices and frameworks to identify suitable, effective safeguards for implementation in Malaysia.
“At the same time, CMCF is conducting a public consultation to develop a Gaming SubCode involving various stakeholders, including app store operators, local and international game developers, online safety experts, the e-sports industry, legal practitioners, and researchers.
“The findings of this study and consultation will serve as the basis to consider evidence-based, risk-proportional regulatory measures to ensure the safety of users, especially children, continues to be safeguarded,” he said  when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027) at the policy stage for the Communications Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Fahmi said the government is also prioritising parental education and awareness, particularly on activating parental control functions on personal devices and online services.
He said this initiative is being carried out through the Safe Internet Campaign, which includes the Parent-Teacher Convention and the Safe Internet Campaign Community Carnival nationwide.
The campaign, allocated RM58.7 million under Budget 2027, targets not only students and children, but also provides education and advocacy programmes for parents, guardians, teachers, and local communities.
This collective approach, he added, ensures that the responsibility of protecting children from online threats is shared across families, educational institutions, communities, government agencies, and service providers.
In a related development, Fahmi said 14,706 instances of pornographic content and child sexual abuse material were taken down, while 5,170 pornographic websites were blocked between Jan 1, 2022, and Sept 30, 2026.
Addressing the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) and deepfakes — specifically the circulation of digitally altered nude images involving schoolgirls in Seremban — he said the case remains under investigation by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), with MCMC collaborating closely with the police and platform provider Meta.
MCMC records also showed that 5,341 complaints concerning cyberbullying and online harassment were lodged between January 1, 2023, and October 15, 2026.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said 828,438 online gambling-related posts and materials were taken down, and 7,411 illegal gambling domains were blocked by service providers following directives from MCMC between January 1, 2022, and September 15, 2026.
Enforcement against illegal gambling has also been stepped up through joint operations with PDRM, including Op JOL and Op Soga XI this year, targeting illegal online bookmaking and betting linked to the 2026 Fifa World Cup.
“MCMC has also enhanced operational cooperation with PDRM and telecommunications service providers through Op Pancing and Op Delusi to curb the large-scale dissemination of short messaging service (SMS) spam using Fake Base Transceiver Station (Fake BTS) equipment containing phishing links to deceive users,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malay reserve land accounts for 91.58pc of titled land in Kelantan, says MB
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 29 — Malay Reserve Land in Kelantan covers 526,083.08 hectares as of June this year, accounting for 91.58 per cent of the total 574,427.61 hectares of titled land recorded in the state, said Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
He told the Kelantan State Assembly today that the figure involved 816,020 land titles.
He said Gua Musang recorded the largest area of Malay Reserve Land, at 122,735.54 hectares or 84.55 per cent of the total titled land in the district.
“For the other districts, Kota Bharu recorded 40,510.49 hectares (99.97 per cent), Pasir Mas 56,656.79 hectares (99.98 per cent), Kuala Krai 53,473.85 hectares (68.73 per cent) and Tumpat 21,607.96 hectares (99.99 per cent).
“Bachok recorded 26,541.25 hectares (99.98 per cent), Tanah Merah 56,246.13 hectares (99.98 per cent), Pasir Puteh 43,377.81 hectares (99.99 per cent), Machang 28,376.83 hectares (96.18 per cent), Jeli 37,240.60 hectares (99.93 per cent) and Lojing 39,315.82 hectares (98.99 per cent),” he said in reply to a question from Datuk Mohd Shabuddin Hashim (BN-Galas).
Mohd Nassuruddin said the state government had always given attention to efforts to maintain the area and status of Malay Reserve Land to ensure that the interests of land ownership among the Malays continued to be protected.
He said all development matters involving Malay Reserve Land must comply with relevant legal provisions, including the Kelantan Malay Reservation Enactment 1930.
“Any development matters involving Malay Reserve Land must comply with the relevant laws to ensure that the development carried out does not result in the erosion of Malay land ownership,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s new vehicle brings geospatial tools together for faster disaster response
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — A Defence Geospatial Information Rapid Team (DGIRT) vehicle has been introduced as a pilot project to accelerate the delivery of geospatial information in the field, supporting defence, security and disaster management operations.
Deputy Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said the vehicle integrates specialised geospatial equipment to enable faster and more accurate field data collection.
“The vehicle will help us obtain more precise information on the ground while expediting response efforts by enabling teams to reach disaster sites more quickly and accelerating the collection of data and information for follow-up action,” he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after launching Defence Geospatial Day 2026 (DG’26), themed “Advancing Defence and Security Through Geospatial Capabilities”, at Wisma Perwira today.
Also present were Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman, Defence Geospatial Division Director Brigadier General Datuk Dr Mohd Zambri Muhammad Rabab, and Deputy Director-General of Survey and Mapping Malaysia (JUPEM) 1 Ahmad Sanusi Che Cob.
Syed Ibrahim said the vehicle, developed by JUPEM in collaboration with the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM), represented a new initiative, although the equipment and instruments it carries had been used previously, including during the landslide incident in Batang Kali, Selangor.
“The difference is that previously, we did not have a dedicated vehicle that integrated all these specific tools. Now, with this combination of equipment, including electric motorcycles and drones, assessments at disaster sites can be carried out with much greater accuracy,” he said.
He added that the initiative drew on lessons from previous disasters and took into account the operational needs of relevant agencies, including the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA).
In his opening address, Syed Ibrahim said geospatial information went beyond mapping, describing it as a strategic national asset essential to strengthening defence preparedness, safeguarding sovereignty and improving the effectiveness of security operations.
He stressed that accurate, integrated and up-to-date information was crucial for supporting decision-making, enhancing situational awareness and ensuring the effective execution of security operations.
At the event, held for the first time in collaboration with JUPEM and ATM, Syed Ibrahim also launched the Defence Geospatial Information Management (DGIM) initiative under the 13th Malaysia Plan (RMK13).
The initiative aims to strengthen the management, integration and sharing of defence-related geospatial information.
He said the development of geospatial capabilities would also involve the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and the exploration of Environmental Intelligence (EI).
Syed Ibrahim further emphasised the importance of cooperation between civilian and military agencies in ensuring coordinated efforts to protect national security and sovereignty, including during humanitarian assistance and disaster management operations. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Malaysian films rake in RM129.9m as local animation pushes deeper into overseas markets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Malaysia’s creative industry continues to gain momentum, with local films and animation recording strong box office earnings and expanding their reach into international markets.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) data as of October 8 showed that 17 films under the Mandatory Screening Scheme had generated combined box office receipts of RM129.86 million.
Among the highest-grossing films were
Tarung: Unforgiven
(RM23.59 million),
Chelot
(RM19.12 million),
Polong
(RM15.05 million),
Libang Libu
(RM14.16 million) and
Malaikat Malam
(RM12.23 million).
In animation, Fahmi said,
Papa Zola The Movie
earned RM63.84 million in Malaysia and more than RM69 million across Southeast Asia as of February 2026, highlighting the regional appeal of Malaysian productions.
“Achievements by
Mechamato Movie
and
Upin & Ipin: Keris Siamang Tunggal
also demonstrate the ability of Malaysian animation to penetrate international markets,” he said when winding up the policy-level debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027) for the Communications Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Fahmi said the commercial success of
Mat Kilau: Kebangkitan Pahlawan
, which grossed RM89.06 million, and
Sheriff: Narko Integriti
(RM59.50 million) further demonstrated the industry’s ability to generate revenue while showcasing Malaysian values, culture and identity.
He said the ministry remained focused on developing local content, intellectual property, market expansion and the competitiveness of Malaysian creative industry players.
Under the 12th Malaysia Plan, the Creative Content Fund (DKK) supported 1,677 local creative projects, generating 32,795 employment opportunities.
To attract international investment, Fahmi said 175 foreign productions chose Malaysia as a filming location between January and July 2026 under the Malaysia: A Filming Destination & Production Hub initiative.
These included
Lord of the Flies
,
Mr VIP
and
Thunderbolts
.
Collaborations with Hasbro Entertainment, producer of
Transformers
, and Banijay Nordic, producer of
Survivor
, also created opportunities for high-skilled employment, knowledge transfer and local companies’ participation in global creative industry supply chains.
Fahmi said the Film in Malaysia Incentive (FIMI) attracted an estimated RM2.75 billion in foreign investment between 2013 and 2025, creating about 31,050 jobs.
Meanwhile, he said Malaysia’s cultural and creative industry contributed RM130.7 billion, or 6.8 per cent, to gross domestic product (GDP) in 2024, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia’s Cultural and Creative Satellite Account 2024.
The sector also supported 763,100 jobs and recorded creative product exports worth RM63 billion (US$15.45 billion).
“Behind every film, musical performance, content production or major event lies a network of workers, businesses and services contributing to the national economy,” he said.
Fahmi added that the government, through MyCreative Ventures (MyCV), continued to provide loans, equity investment and market access through initiatives such as Kembara RIUH to help creative entrepreneurs expand their businesses.
He cited local men’s footwear and fashion brand Zeve, a MyCV financing recipient, which recorded RM10 million in revenue in 2025. The company’s monthly sales rose from RM30,000 to RM1.1 million, while its workforce expanded from one employee to 52. — Bernama

Title: Bersatu signs confidence and supply pact with Madani govt, says MPs to get same allocations as govt backbenchers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Bersatu has signed a confidence and supply agreement (CSA) with the Madani government, pledging its support for the Supply Bill 2027, or Budget 2027,
The Star
reported.
According to the English daily, Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the agreement would allow the party’s MPs to receive the same constituency development allocations as government backbenchers.
“I signed on behalf of Bersatu and there are also the other six who previously showed support to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“There are also matters concerning institutional reforms, including proposals to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure to a maximum of two terms and to separate the powers of the Attorney General.
“In return, the government has decided to provide our MPs with the same constituency development allocations as government MPs,” he told reporters after the signing ceremony at Parliament.
Muhyiddin said the agreement followed a similar arrangement during the administration of former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, when Anwar was the opposition leader.
“Its sole purpose is to create a more stable situation in the country so that important matters affecting the people, particularly the economy and cost of living, can continue to be addressed.
“With this agreement, stability can help the government manage the country more effectively. We, particularly Bersatu and the opposition, will continue to fulfil our responsibility to provide checks and balances.
“This agreement does not mean we are giving up our responsibility as the opposition. We remain the opposition,” he was quoted as saying.
Asked what would happen if either side breached the agreement, Muhyiddin said the terms provided for such a situation, the report said.
“If something has been agreed upon but is not adhered to, the party concerned, whether the government or the political party, may take action, which could lead to the termination of the CSA we signed today,” he was quoted as saying.
Asked why Bersatu had signed the agreement now, nearly a year before Parliament is due to be dissolved, Muhyiddin said the party had hoped for such an arrangement from the beginning.
“Today, I am the only one who has signed it. There are one or two other parties on the opposition side, and I do not know why they have not entered into an agreement. That is their issue.
“From the beginning, we had asked for all MPs to be given equal allocations. When I was prime minister, allocations were given to all MPs, from both the government and the opposition.
“But under the current Prime Minister, he said perhaps the time had not yet come. Today, that time has come,” he said.
The Star
reported that Muda’s Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman was also involved in the signing, which was facilitated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
Also present were Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
Bersatu vice-president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu, Putrajaya MP Datuk Radzi Jidin and Langkawi MP Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah were among those attending the ceremony, according to the report.

Title: Skip toll payments and risk being tracked under new MLFF system, says works minister
Article:
PORT KLANG, Oct 29 — The full implementation of the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) toll collection system is expected to help address the issue of toll evasion, including by identifying motorists who commit such offences.
Minister of Works Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the Ministry of Works (KKR), through the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), continuously monitors the efficiency and effectiveness of toll systems nationwide which are developed by highway concession companies.
He noted that initiatives currently being implemented by these concession companies include toll payment technology based on Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR), which is aimed, among other things, at reducing traffic congestion.
“Therefore, the implementation of the Multi-Lane Fast Flow (MLFF) system at toll plaza lanes will also assist in obtaining information regarding individuals who commit toll evasion.
“This, in turn, facilitates the tracking of such offenders and enables claims to be made against them should they evade detection,” he said at the launch ceremony for the Westports-Public Works Department (JKR) Klang Road Safety CSR Initiative at West Port, here today.
On October 23, the media reported that the concessionaire and operator of the Kuala Lumpur–Karak Expressway (KLK) and the East Coast Expressway Phase 1 (LPT1) incur losses over RM20,000 annually due to persistent toll evasion.
AFA Systems and Services Sdn Bhd general manager, Ismaliza Ibrahim was reported as saying that his organization records approximately 3,000 instances of toll evasion per year with an average of eight cases daily.
On October 13, Alexander said artificial intelligence (AI) technology would be incorporated into the MLFF system once it is fully implemented.
Under Section 8 of the Federal Roads (Private Management) Act 1984, individuals found guilty of toll evasion face a fine of no less than RM2,000 and no more than RM5,000, or imprisonment for up to one year.
Alexander acknowledged that toll evasion has been an ongoing issue though it involves a relatively small number of cases and noted that his team is currently working closely with enforcement agencies, such as the Road Transport Department (JPJ) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), to address the matter.
Regarding preparations for Northeast Monsoon season (MTL), Nanta said his ministry is in a state of full readiness, which includes enhancing the effectiveness of the Disaster Operations Room (BiGBen).
“Through this operations room, we remain prepared to conduct monitoring to identify any disasters particularly floods in affected locations,” he said.
Meanwhile, Nanta noted that the primary objective of the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) programme with Westports is to improve awareness and safety within the port area, which sees the daily movement of nearly 80,000 vehicles, including a large number of heavy machines.
“Measures include the installation of road studs, rumble strips, and warning signs, as well as the implementation of proper lighting, road markings, and effective speed management.
“Furthermore, we are considering a proposal to provide dedicated lanes or paths for motorcyclists, who account for the highest number of accident victims in the area,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sabah targets RM100b GDP by 2030 through investment, industrial growth, says CM
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 29 — Sabah is pursuing various initiatives to achieve a gross domestic product (GDP) target of RM100 billion by 2030 under its Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) development agenda, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the state government was focusing on implementing industrial development plans, attracting investments and providing essential infrastructure, including a stable, reliable and affordable energy supply.
“When investors consider building a factory or conducting large-scale operations in Sabah, they need to know whether we can provide an adequate supply of electricity and gas, what the costs will be, and when such supplies can be made available,” he said.
The text of his speech was read out by Assistant Minister to the Chief Minister Datuk Ceasar Mandela Malakun at the opening of the Sabah Energy Corporation (SEC) Annual Planning Conference here today.
Hajiji said Sabah’s gas supply had the potential to increase from approximately 700 million standard cubic feet per day to 1,350 million standard cubic feet per day by 2030, based on the Long-Term Gas Supply and Transmission Plan presented to the state government last September.
He added that the proposed development of gas resources along Sabah’s east coast would create new opportunities for power generation and industrial growth in the region.
Hajiji also highlighted progress in strengthening Sabah’s participation in the energy sector through the Commercial Collaboration Agreement (CCA) with Petronas, signed in December 2021.
He commended SEC’s financial performance and its efforts to expand operations through the Progressive Energy Transformation Agenda (PETA 2030).
He also called on government-linked companies (GLCs) and state agencies to enhance cooperation to accelerate project implementation and prevent investment opportunities from being lost. — Bernama

Title: Hajiji: Sabah allocates RM98.06m to empower youth, boost role in policymaking
Article:
TUARAN, Oct 29 — The Sabah government is strengthening youth participation in policymaking through initiatives such as the Chief Minister’s Young Thinkers (Pemikir Muda) initiative and the Sabah Youth Assembly, providing platforms for young people to contribute ideas on the state’s development.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said youths were not only future leaders but also key economic drivers and agents of change in realising the aspirations of the Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) development plan.
“Youth are a vital asset in determining the direction and future of Sabah. Therefore, the Chief Minister’s Young Thinkers initiative provides a space for Sabah’s youth to be directly involved in the formulation of state development policies.
“Meanwhile, the Sabah Youth Assembly serves as a platform for youth unity and representation, providing a space to discuss issues and the future of the young generation under a new implementation format overseen by the relevant ministry,” he said.
He was speaking at the Tuaran Youth Tamu Carnival here today.
Hajiji said RM98.06 million had been allocated to the state’s Ministry of Youth Development, Sports Advancement and Creative Economy this year to empower young people through various forms of assistance, funding and skills training.
He said the allocation covered human capital development, grants for youth associations, support for the sports sector and assistance for young entrepreneurs through the Sabah Youth Entrepreneur Success Scheme (Syabas).
It also included the Rumah Mesra SMJ initiative, which provides support for young people who have recently started families.
Hajiji added that the state government was strengthening youth skills through Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) to meet the needs of future industries and nurture a generation capable of creating employment opportunities.
On the Tuaran Youth Tamu Carnival, he said the event highlighted the role of young people as future leaders in society and the state, as well as strategic partners in advancing economic, social and community development.
He said the carnival drew on the traditional tamu concept, which brings together traders, small-scale entrepreneurs, farmers, artists and local communities, while providing young people with opportunities to exchange ideas, showcase their talents, expand their businesses and build collaborative networks.
“When the tamu concept is combined with the energy and creativity of youth, a more dynamic space is created for entrepreneurial, cultural, sporting and wholesome entertainment activities, as well as knowledge-sharing,” he said.
Hajiji expressed hope that the carnival would continue to provide opportunities for young people to promote local products, showcase their artistic and cultural talents, build self-confidence and expand their business and community networks. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan tables RM1.38b Budget 2027 with RM4.31m operating deficit
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 29 — The Kelantan state government today tabled a RM1.383 billion Budget 2027, comprising RM1.087 billion in operating expenditure and RM296 million for development.
Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud said the budget focused on four key pillars, namely strengthening religion and human capital development; social welfare and public protection; a progressive and resilient economy; and environmental sustainability and urban beautification.
He said state revenue for 2027 was projected at RM1.082 billion, comprising RM238.8 million in tax revenue, RM314.5 million in non-tax revenue, and RM529.29 million in non-revenue receipts.
“The difference between projected revenue and operating expenditure indicates a deficit of RM4.31 million.
“This requires consistent fiscal discipline through expenditure controls, stronger revenue collection and a reassessment of less urgent projects,” he said when tabling the budget at the State Assembly sitting here today.
Mohd Nassuruddin said the state government would prioritise spending that safeguarded public welfare, supported essential services and delivered long-term economic benefits despite limited fiscal space.
He said spending decisions must consider financial capacity, project readiness and implementation capabilities.
“Land-related revenue is projected at RM373.57 million, forestry revenue at RM70.4 million and mining revenue at RM48.41 million.
“State resources must be managed to ensure fair returns, regulatory compliance, and environmental protection. At the same time, existing revenue collection must be improved to ensure the state’s rightful dues are collected efficiently,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Penang awaits full report on fatal Paya Terubong landslide as probe continues
Article:
BATU KAWAN, Oct 29 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has submitted a draft technical report on the recent landslide at Taman Seri Permai, Paya Terubong, to the state government, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
He said the report was still being followed up and reviewed before a detailed report on the incident could be finalised.
“Several possible causes of the incident have been identified for further investigation by the technical authorities, including weather conditions, surface runoff, drainage pipes and excessive soil load.
“However, we do not want to speculate. A detailed explanation should come from the engineers, and the state government is also still awaiting the full report from MBPP on the incident,” he told reporters after opening Estek Automation’s new factory here today.
In the incident at 8.36am last Sunday, a 73-year-old doctor, Wong Kar Lin, was killed after being buried in a landslide that hit his home.
Chow said matters related to technical planning would be handled by state Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye, while the welfare of affected residents would be coordinated by state Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai, who is also the Paya Terubong assemblyman.
He said the developer had been in contact with the affected residents to assess their accommodation and welfare needs.
Commenting on calls for the state government to halt all development projects involving high-risk slopes, Chow said such a move could have legal implications as the developers had obtained the relevant approvals and commenced work.
He said project approvals were granted based on procedures and conditions stipulated by the relevant authorities and agencies, including technical agencies.
Meanwhile, Chow said the state government had directed all relevant agencies to remain on standby throughout the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), particularly in anticipation of possible flooding following heavy rain.
He said September to November was typically a period of high rainfall in Penang, and all agencies therefore needed to take appropriate action based on information received from the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) whenever it rained.
The 2026/2027 MTL began on October 27 and will continue until March 2027. According to the Malaysian Meteorological Department, three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain are expected from November this year to January 2027.
This could increase the risk of flooding, particularly in areas near rivers and low-lying areas, while strong winds could also cause rough seas and rising sea levels in the waters of the South China Sea. — Bernama

Title: South China Sea territorial contest a test of Asean’s unity and credibility, says Mohamed Khaled
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Asean member states should not allow overlapping maritime claims in the South China Sea to fracture the peace and solidarity in the region, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
Speaking at the 20th Asean Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM), Mohamed Khaled said the Asean solidarity is one of the bloc’s greatest strengths that must be preserved.
“The South China Sea represents one of the most consequential tests of Asean’s unity, credibility, and commitment to its founding principles,” Mohamed Khaled told his Asean counterparts in Cebu, the Philippines yesterday.
“Several member states have overlapping maritime claims, and each has legitimate interests in safeguarding its sovereignty and territorial rights.
“But no dispute, however deeply rooted, should be allowed to fracture Asean or undermine the peace we have spent decades building,” he said.
Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Brunei, China and Vietnam have competing claims over territories in the contested waters.
Asean and China signed a non-binding Declaration on the Conduct of Parties (DoC) in 2002 and talks for a binding Code of Conduct (CoC) have been underway since 2013. Both parties are reportedly expecting to finalise the CoC by end of this year.
Stronger regional disaster response capability needed
As the region increasingly grapple with the ravages of climate change, Mohamed Khaled said Asean requires a stronger, more coordinated and effective regional disaster response capability.
He pointed out that Asean already has essential mechanisms in place, such as the Asean Militaries Ready Group on Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (AMRG on HADR).
Asean Defence Ministers’ pose for the symbolic Asean handshake at the 20th Asean Defence Ministers’ Meeting in Cebu, the Philippines. — Picture courtesy of Ministry of Defence (Mindef)
The mechanism provides a framework to coordinate military assistance and facilitate the deployment of military assets to disaster-affected areas, which was reflected in Asean’s response to the devastating earthquake in Myanmar last year.
“We must now build upon these foundations to strengthen operational readiness, improve coordination and ensure that our armed forces can respond swiftly and effectively when disasters strike,” he said.
Confronting new threats
Established in 2006, the ADMM marked its 20th anniversary this year under the chairmanship of the Philippines with the theme “Navigating Our Future, Together”.
As such, Mohamed Khaled called on the ADMM to develop strong local and regional capacity to respond to new non-traditional threats effectively.
“The threats confronting Asean today are more complex, more interconnected, and potentially more destructive than ever before.
“We must acknowledge that non-traditional threats are no longer distant possibilities. These threats are real, recurring and increasingly difficult to ignore,” he said.
Mohamed Khaled also reminded his counterparts that Asean member states cannot effectively combat the evolving security challenges by working in silos.
“No Asean member state, regardless of its resources, can address these challenges entirely on its own.
“Asean’s future cannot be secured by any one member state acting alone.
“Our strength rests on the trust we build among ourselves, our willingness to manage differences constructively, and our determination to uphold the wider interests of the region,” he added.

Title: KTMB offers record 1.57 million ETS, ERT seats for January to March 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is offering a record 1,573,872 seats for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and Ekspres Rakyat Timuran (ERT) from January to March 2027, a 39 per cent increase over the same period this year.
In a statement today, KTMB said ticket sales for both services will open in stages from November 2, allowing the public to plan travel ahead of school holidays, public holidays and festive seasons.
Ticket sales for ETS and ERT travel between January and February 2027 will open at noon on November 2, while tickets for March 2027 travel will go on sale on December 1.
According to the statement, of the total seats on offer, 1,520,592 are allocated to ETS and 53,280 to ERT.
“The figure exceeds the 1,131,500 seats offered for the same period in 2026, making it the highest number KTMB has ever provided for the first three months of the following year,” the statement read.
“This increase in capacity reflects KTMB’s ongoing efforts to provide more travel options to meet the needs of rail service users,” it said.
ETS ridership is projected to grow 6.5 per cent to 6.28 million passengers in 2027 from 5.9 million this year, matching the capacity increase.
With demand rising, KTMB will increase ETS service frequency in 2027 from 44 scheduled services a day in 2026 to 50 services a day from Monday to Thursday and 58 services a day from Friday to Sunday, an increase of between six and 14 services a day.
The higher frequency also covers the JB Sentral- KL Sentral- JB Sentral route, where services will rise from eight to 12 a day.
The move is expected to offer passengers more schedule options, particularly on weekends and during peak seasons.
In addition, KTM announced that the Old Kuala Lumpur Station and Subang Jaya Station will become additional ETS hubs, widening rail access and offering alternative stations to ease congestion at KL Sentral during peak hours and busy seasons.
In a related move, KTMB will restructure its long-distance ETS timetable from Jan 1, 2027, affecting several routes linking the northern and southern sectors of the network.
“Direct through-travel on the same train for the JB Sentral-Butterworth, JB Sentral-Padang Besar and Butterworth-Segamat routes, and in the reverse direction, will no longer be offered. Passengers on these routes must change trains at KL Sentral,” the statement said.
KTMB said tickets for long-distance ETS services requiring a train change at KL Sentral must currently be bought in two separate transactions, one per travel sector.
However, KTMB is upgrading its booking system to allow integrated purchases in a single transaction from December.
Passengers are therefore advised to check schedules for both ETS services and ensure sufficient transfer time at KL Sentral before booking.
The public is encouraged to buy tickets early via the KITS Style app or the official KTMB website at www.ktmb.com.my, and to check the latest schedules before booking, particularly for long-distance trips requiring a train change at KL Sentral. — Bernama

Title: Sultan Nazrin tells Dewan Negara Perak members, palace dignitaries not to exploit royal ties for profit
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR, Oct 29 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, has warned members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court against misusing the Ruler’s name, royal influence and their titles for personal gain, financial profit or business opportunities.
His Royal Highness also urged them not to allow themselves to be used to assist parties in an improper or questionable manner, or to exert undue pressure on anyone.
“Shun corruption, the abuse of power and any conduct that might give rise to suspicion or tarnish the reputation of the throne and the Royal Court.
“Never allow your position to become a means of seeking special privileges, accumulating personal wealth or interfering in matters beyond the scope of your responsibilities,” he decreed at the 175th Meeting of Dewan Negara Perak at Istana Iskandariah here today.
Sultan Nazrin also urged members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court to remain vigilant and exercise sound judgement in communications, particularly when using social media channels and platforms.
“...exercise care and discretion in both word and deed. Matters entrusted to you in confidence must be safeguarded. Information whose accuracy has yet to be established must not be circulated.
“Opinions should be expressed with due propriety, without giving rise to slander or discord. In today’s world, a single remark or recording shared on social media can give rise to many different interpretations,” he said.
His Royal Highness also called on them to avoid disputes, power struggles and factionalism while maintaining close ties with the people.
He said public grievances must be heard and addressed, particularly those involving vulnerable groups such as senior citizens, persons with disabilities, orphans, low-income families and marginalised communities.
“Maintain good relations with people from every walk of life. Our State is home to people of diverse ethnicities, religions and backgrounds. Respect this diversity and work towards strengthening unity, in accordance with the Constitution and the law,” he said.
Sultan Nazrin said members of Dewan Negara Perak and royal dignitaries must understand the role of the monarchy within the framework of a constitutional monarchy.
“Respect the prescribed limits of authority and responsibility. Work professionally with the government and state institutions, without interfering in administrative affairs or using your position to advance partisan political interests,” he said.
The Sultan also encouraged them to continuously broaden their knowledge and improve their ways of working, understand societal changes, and make prudent use of technology.
The Sultan further stressed that every palace dignitary must set an example for their families, officers, staff and the wider community.
“Show that those who are close to the Ruler are equally committed to their responsibilities, and that those who are accorded honour also know how to honour others,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal allows lawyer Rosli Dahlan to challenge police, prosecution seizure of four ASNB accounts
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 29 — The Court of Appeal today granted lawyer Rosli Dahlan leave to commence a judicial review challenging the police and public prosecutor’s move to seize his four Amanah Saham Nasional Bhd (ASNB) accounts under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLA).
A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, Datuk Nadzarin Wok Nordin and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar unanimously allowed Rosli’s appeal to overturn a High Court decision that had dismissed his leave application.
The appellate bench ordered the case remitted to the High Court for a full hearing on its substantive merits before a different judge or judicial commissioner.
Delivering the court’s decision, Justice Choo held that the High Court had erred in disallowing Rosli’s application for leave to initiate the judicial review.
Justice Choo said the court was of the view that the High Court judge had applied a level of scrutiny more appropriate to a substantive hearing than to a leave application.
He also said Rosli had demonstrated a prima facie arguable case that the seizure orders may have been affected by mala fide, collateral purpose, irrationality or abuse of power.
“Whether those allegations can ultimately be established is a matter for a substantive hearing. The learned High Court judge therefore erred in refusing leave for this preliminary stage,” Justice Choo said.
Rosli’s lawyer Harvinderjit Singh confirmed the court’s decision to Bernama when contacted.
On August 14, 2024, the then High Court judge Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh (now Chief Justice) dismissed Rosli’s application for leave to initiate the judicial review.
In his application filed in December 2023, Rosli named several respondents, including former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain, Commercial Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Seri Ramli Mohammed Yoosuf, the Royal Malaysia Police, former Attorney-General Datuk Ahmad Terrirudin Mohd Salleh, deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Zulfadli Mohd Nawawi and the Malaysian government.
Rosli is seeking, among other things, a certiorari order to quash the decision or action of the respondents who issued or caused the issuance of the seizure orders under Section 50 of the AMLA Act 2001.
At today’s proceedings, the Attorney-General’s Chambers was represented by senior federal counsel Normastura Ayub and federal counsel Zulkiefli Sulaiman.
Also representing Rosli were lawyers Chetan Jethwani, Amiratu Al Amirat, Ho Yu Fei and Shavitta Devi Raja Mohan. — Bernama

Title: Sabah’s 40pc revenue rights appeal: Court of Appeal to decide on Nov 12
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 29 — The Court of Appeal will determine on November 12 when it will deliver its ruling on the federal government’s appeal against parts of a High Court decision on Sabah’s 40 per cent net revenue entitlement for 1974 to 2021.
The three-judge panel comprising Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Ahmad Kamal Md Shahid and Datuk Amarjeet Singh Serjit Singh fixed the date for e-Review case management after hearing submissions from the federal government, the Sabah Law Society (SLS) and the Sabah government today.
The panel said it needed more time to consider the submissions before delivering its decision.
The federal government is challenging parts of the Kota Kinabalu High Court ruling, including findings that both the federal and Sabah governments had abused their powers and breached their constitutional responsibilities.
However, SLS said the federal government’s notice of appeal did not challenge the 40 per cent constitutional formula or the need for a review under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution. Its appeal nevertheless challenges findings and orders concerning the “Lost Years”, the review process, the relief granted and the High Court’s jurisdiction.
During the hearing, Senior Federal Counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly @ Arwi argued that the High Court had erred in finding that the federal government breached its constitutional duties and in issuing an order compelling a review of Sabah’s special grant.
The federal government maintained that the 1970 First Review Order remained legally in force until it was superseded by a 2022 Review Order, relying on Article 112D(3) of the Federal Constitution. It contended that payments made to Sabah between 1974 and 2021 were constitutional and challenged the High Court’s jurisdiction to hear the case.
Representing SLS, lawyer David Fung Yin Kee argued that no constitutional review had been conducted between 1974 and 2021, as required under Article 112D. He said correspondence and meetings between the two governments did not constitute a formal review under the Constitution.
Fung also defended SLS’s right to bring the judicial review in the public interest, arguing that the courts could intervene where constitutional obligations had not been fulfilled.
The Sabah government broadly supported the High Court’s finding that no review had been conducted since the first review in 1969. However, it opposed quashing the interim review arrangements for 2022, 2023 and 2024, arguing that they should remain in force while the constitutional issues are resolved.
On October 17 last year, High Court judge Datuk Celestina Stuel Galid allowed a judicial review application by SLS and ordered the federal government to review Sabah’s 40 per cent revenue entitlement with the state government for the financial years from 1974 to 2021, a period known as the “Lost Years”.
The court ordered the review to be completed within 90 days and the two governments to reach an agreement within 180 days.
The federal government subsequently obtained a stay of the order from the Court of Appeal in Putrajaya on April 6, pending its appeal.
The federal government was represented by Senior Federal Counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly @ Arwi and Nurhafizza Azizan, together with Azza Azmi, Safiyyah Omar and Nur Atirah Aiman Rahim.
SLS was represented by David Fung Yin Kee, Jeyan T.M. Marimuttu, Janice Junie Lim, Liew Yung Enn and Vanessa Maria Marimuttu.
The Sabah government was represented by State Attorney-General Datuk Brenndon Keith Soh, Senior State Counsel Mohd Saifurrazee Mohamed @ Hussin and Devina Teo, and State Counsel Roland Alik.

Title: IWK suspects dislocated joint on 30-year-old pipe caused Bayan Baru sinkhole, repairs due Nov 7
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 29 — Indah Water Konsortium Sdn Bhd (IWK) has launched an immediate investigation into a sinkhole incident along Lebuhraya Mayang Pasir in Bayan Baru here, which is suspected to have been caused by a dislocated sewer pipe joint.
In a statement today, IWK said its site investigation began immediately after it received public complaints about the incident, and emergency repair works to restore the affected sewerage infrastructure have also been initiated, with completion targeted for November 7, 2026, weather permitting.
“Based on preliminary findings, the incident is suspected to have been caused by a dislocated pipe joint. The affected sewer pipe is approximately 300 millimetres (mm) in diameter, located at a depth of about four metres and is more than 30 years old,” it said.
IWK said this was the first reported incident of its kind in the area, with no previous complaints related to sewer defects recorded.
The company said detailed investigations would continue, alongside close monitoring of the site, to determine the actual cause of the incident, and that the situation was under control, with immediate protective measures put in place at the affected area.
IWK said it conducted periodic scheduled inspections as part of its risk management approach to sewerage infrastructure and it was also undertaking comprehensive closed-circuit television (CCTV) inspections and ground-penetrating radar (GPR) scanning across Penang to assess ageing infrastructure and identify areas requiring sewer pipeline upgrading works.
IWK reiterated its commitment to safeguarding public safety, minimising environmental impact and working closely with the relevant authorities and stakeholders to restore the affected infrastructure promptly and responsibly.
It said the site would continue to be monitored closely, with the necessary support provided until restoration works were completed.
A 2.5-metre-wide and four-metre-deep sinkhole appeared on Lebuhraya Mayang Pasir in Bayan Baru near here today, believed to be caused by damage to the IWK sewerage drainage system.
State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said a Public Works Department (JKR) investigation indicated the sinkhole likely stemmed from a displaced pipe joint. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia stands in solidarity with Saudi Arabia, condemns Houthi attacks, says Khaled Nordin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Malaysia has expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid its current security challenges and affirmed its readiness to assist within its capabilities.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said he conveyed the message during a telephone conversation with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, yesterday.
Mohamed Khaled said he received the call while attending the 20th Asean Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) in Cebu, the Philippines, following an earlier telephone conversation between the two ministers last month.
“Malaysia stands in solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid its current security challenges and remains ready to assist within our capabilities. May Saudi Arabia and its people remain safe and secure, insya-Allah,” he posted on his official X account.
Meanwhile, Prince Khalid said in a separate post on X that the two ministers reviewed bilateral defence relations and discussed regional developments during the conversation.
He said they also condemned attacks by the Houthi militia against Saudi Arabia and the holy sites.
King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was previously targeted in attacks that caused multiple deaths and injuries, prompting Saudi authorities to temporarily suspend airport operations. The airport partially reopened on Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Malaysians arrested on drug charges in 40 countries, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Forty countries have recorded the arrest of Malaysian citizens in drug-related cases, with intensified enforcement in those countries among the factors driving greater attention to such offences, said Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni.
He said Malaysia is working to clarify the situation with those countries, given its perceived high numbers in drug cases, which in turn have prompted tighter enforcement abroad.
He also noted that cross-border drug smuggling methods are becoming more sophisticated, making the activity harder to curb and requiring close cooperation between enforcement agencies and countries.
“The techniques for smuggling drugs into those countries are growing more sophisticated and diverse,” he said in reply to a supplementary question from Datuk Seri Doris Sophia Brodi (GPS-Sri Aman) in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Doris Sophia asked about the government’s initiatives and diplomatic cooperation through Asean and strategic partner countries to curb cross-border criminal syndicates, such as fake job offers and paid luggage-carrying schemes containing drugs.
In that regard, Lukanisman said Malaysia will leverage the Asean platform to strengthen discussions on cross-border drug crime, including through future multilateral conferences.
He said efforts to curb drug mule activities involve not only the Foreign Ministry through Wisma Putra but also various government agencies, particularly enforcement ones.
He noted that Wisma Putra’s role covers consular assistance after Malaysians are detained abroad, including helping them follow the prescribed procedures and informing their families.
Meanwhile, Lukanisman said Malaysia is refining cooperation with Thailand and Indonesia on transferring offenders to resolve legal issues involving prisoners through diplomatic channels.
He said the discussions are being carried out through diplomatic relations, including engagement with the ambassadors of the countries concerned.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Dr Halimah Ali (PN-Kapar) on which countries Malaysia is negotiating with for an international prisoner transfer agreement, following the signing of the International Transfer of Prisoners Treaty (ITOP) with Pakistan on August 21.
Halimah also raised the possibility of prisoners convicted abroad serving the remainder of their sentences in Malaysia under the International Transfer of Prisoners Act 2012. — Bernama

Title: Armizan: Domestic Trade Ministry weighs Nibong Tebal petrol station licence suspension after RM270,000 subsidy misuse detected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) will suspend or revoke a petrol station’s Control of Supplies Act (CSA) licence in Nibong Tebal, Penang if it is found misusing the BUDI Madani petrol subsidy.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the government could take such action under the Control of Supplies Act 1961 if the petrol station breaches licensing conditions, including manipulating transaction records or misappropriating government subsidies.
He said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) is currently conducting investigations, with KPDN involved.
“On KPDN’s part, should they be found guilty later, among the actions we can take is to suspend or cancel the CSA licence of the station owner under the Control of Supplies Act.
“To operate a petrol station, besides a licence under the Petroleum Development Act 1974 (PDA), one must also have a CSA licence for scheduled controlled goods,” he said at a special news conference announcing the 2026 Deepavali Festive Season Maximum Price Scheme (SHMMP) here today.
Deputy Minister of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh was also present.
Armizan said the government will not compromise on any misappropriation of the BUDI Madani subsidy because the programme involves a large financial commitment to assist the public.
On Tuesday, the Ministry of Finance (MoF) said it blocked a petrol station in Sungai Buaya, Nibong Tebal, from selling subsidised RON95 petrol and diesel under BUDI Madani after detecting suspicious subsidy misuse transactions.
According to MoF, a review of the petrol station’s transaction records revealed over 1,000 transactions using manual bypass methods, involving more than 100,000 litres of petrol with a government subsidy value exceeding RM270,000. — Bernama

Title: Report: Bersatu to sign confidence and supply agreement with Madani govt this evening
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) will sign a confidence and supply agreement (CSA) with the Madani government this evening,
Sinar Harian
reported.
The Malay daily said a party leader confirmed the matter when contacted today.
However, details of the signing ceremony, the terms of the agreement and the MPs involved have yet to be disclosed, with a press conference expected to be held on the matter.
An online news portal reported that the signing would take place at the office of Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof,
Sinar Harian
added.
According to the report, the agreement covers all 19 MPs who remain with Bersatu and is meant to guarantee support for Budget 2027 should Barisan Nasional (BN) withdraw its backing.
Under the agreement, the MPs are expected to receive allocations for their respective constituencies from next year.
The pact is believed to be aimed at providing additional support to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s administration, particularly during the vote on Budget 2027.
The report said the CSA could alter the balance of support in the Dewan Rakyat and reduce the government’s reliance on BN votes.
A CSA typically involves an agreement to back the government on matters of confidence and supply, including the Budget, without necessarily joining the administration.

Title: Melaka polls: PKR adds Ayer Limau, to contest 10 seats, says Fuziah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) has added one more state seat to its list for the upcoming Melaka state election, bringing its total to 10 seats up from the nine previously announced.
PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the additional seat is the Ayer Limau constituency, which will be contested by the party’s candidate, Major (Rtd) Jaimi Dimon.
She noted that this addition brings the total number of seats to be contested by Pakatan Harapan (PH) to 22 so far an increase from the 21 previously announced though this remains subject to any changes involving other parties.
“Yesterday, we issued the letters of appointment (candidacy papers), and we have since added one more seat to our list. When we announced our candidates previously, it was for nine seats; today, we have added another, bringing the total number of seats to be contested by PKR to 10.
“As it stands, there are 22 (PH candidates), unless other parties also make additions as we didn’t finalise it that day, but since PKR felt we could add one more seat, we brought the total to 10 seats,” she said.
Fuziah, who is also the Deputy Minister of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living, made these remarks after attending a special press conference held by the Minister of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living, Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali, here today on the implementation of the Deepavali Festive Season Maximum Price Scheme for 2026.
Regarding preparations for the state election, Fuziah said she had visited all of PKR’s main operations centres in the state constituencies the party is contesting, and expressed satisfaction with the readiness of the election machinery.
“So far, I am satisfied with their preparations covering everything from the election machinery, polling districts, and operations centres to data and logistics and they are ready for nomination day this Saturday,” she said.
The Melaka State Legislative Assembly was dissolved on September 23. The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as the polling day for the Melaka state election, with nomination day scheduled for October 31 and early voting for November 10.
A total of 687,697 voters are eligible to cast their ballots in the state election. — Bernama

Title: Johor DoE probes white effluent in Sungai Kim Kim, checks CCTV after pollution fears resurface
Article:
PASIR GUDANG, Oct 29 — The Department of Environment (DoE) is investigating Sungai Kim Kim here after receiving reports of a white cloudy effluent, triggering fears that pollution has returned.
The effluent, spotted near the bypass road between Taman Pasir Putih and Kota Masai here, is suspected of causing a foul odour reported since yesterday that has affected various areas around Johor Bahru and Pasir Gudang.
Johor Department of Environment (DoE) director Dr. Mohd Famey Yusoff said that the department has launched an investigation after receiving complaints about the incident.
“However, the river was found to have returned to normal and was no longer white or cloudy by the time DoE officers arrived at the scene to conduct an inspection.
“Therefore, it is likely that the incident occurred due to a one-off dumping of harmful substances into the river,” he told reporters when contacted about the issue today.
Earlier, residents in affected areas of Pasir Gudang took to social media to express frustration over the cloudy white effluent, which they say has occurred multiple times.
White cloudy effluent seen in Sungai Kim Kim near the Taman Pasir Putih–Kota Masai bypass road in Pasir Gudang on October 29, 2026, raising fears of renewed pollution. — Picture via Facebook
They have also urged the authorities to take stern action against those responsible.
On follow-up operations, Mohd Famey said that the Johor DoE, in collaboration with the Pasir Gudang City Council (MBPG), will examine closed-circuit television (CCTV) camera footage from the affected area to identify those responsible.
He added that action would be taken against any party found to have caused the pollution in accordance with relevant legal provisions.
On September 9, the High Court ruled in favour of 171 plaintiffs in their civil suit against four defendants over the previous Sungai Kim Kim incident.
Judicial Commissioner Manira Mohd Nor delivered the ruling and ordered the four defendants — a used tyre processing plant, P Tech Resources Sdn Bhd; two company directors who are Singaporean nationals, Wang Jing Chao, 41, and Yap Yoke Liang, 43; and a lorry driver, N. Maridass, 42 — to pay legal costs of RM100,000 to the plaintiffs.
